e0665e311f.d: By His yoga shakti, Shri Shankara Bhagavatpada went to Kailasa. There, Samba Parameshvara blessed Him with five sphatika linga-s by name Yoga, Bhoga, Vara, Siddhi and Mukti (and called Chandramaulishvara) and Saundarya Lahari, the Devi stotra par excellence. Bhagavan ordained to Bhagavatpada that puja should be done thrice daily to the linga-s with different kinds of abhisheka and naivedya, for the world to attain all shreyas. Among those lingas, the Yoga Linga idol is worshipped by our Kamakoti Acharyas themselves, and Devi Mahātripurasundari is worshipped as a Shrichakra Meru. Shri Bhagavatpāda installed the other linga-s at Kedara, Nepal, Tungabhadra Sangama and Chidambara. This is known by many pramana grantha-s such as Shiva Rahasya and Markandeya Samhitā. The Shrimatham tradition is that Chandramaulishvara came to us on Magha Shukla Panchami, and therefore, there is a special naivedyam performed on this occasion in Shri Matham.

e0f44c3020.d: The massacre of the Hindu population in Noakhali started on 10 October, on the day of Kojagari Lakshmi Puja.  It is estimated that 5,000 were killed, hundreds of Hindu women were raped and thousands of Hindu men and women were forcibly converted to Islam. Around 50,000 to 75,000 survivors were sheltered in temporary relief camps in Comilla, Chandpur, Agartala and other places. Around 50,000 Hindus remained marooned in the affected areas under the strict surveillance of the Muslims, where the administration had no say. According to Dinesh Chandra, Hindus were forced to pay subscriptions to the Muslim League and jiziyah.

e1fdc4b935.d:
Chāpekar brothers killed W. C. Rand.

On 22 June 1897, the Diamond Jubilee of the coronation of Queen Victoria was celebrated in Pune. In his autobiography Damodar Hari writes that he believed the jubilee celebrations would cause Europeans of all ranks to go to the Government House, and give them the opportunity to kill Rand. The brothers Damodar Hari and Balkrishna Hari selected a spot of Ganeshkhind road, by side of a yellow bungalow to shoot at Rand. Each armed with a sword and a pistol. Balkrishna in addition carried a hatchet. They reached Ganeshkhind, they saw what looked like Rand’s carriage pass by, but they let it go, not being sure, deciding to attack him on his way back. They reached Government House at 7.00 – 7.30 in the evening, the sun had set and darkness began to set in. A large number of people had gathered to witness the spectacle at the Government House. There were bonfires on the hills. The swords and the hatchets they carried made movement without raising suspicion difficult, so they cached them under a stone culvert near the bungalow. As planned, Damodar Hari waited at the gate of the Government House, and as Rand’s carriage emerged, ran 10 – 15 paces behind it. As the carriage reached the yellow bungalow, Damodar made up the distance, and called out “Gondya ala re”, a predetermined signal for Balkrishna to take action. Damodar Hari undid the flap of the carriage, raised it and fired from a distance of about a span. It was originally planned that both would shoot at Rand, so as to ensure that Rand would not live, however Balkrishna Hari lagged behind and Rand’s carriage rolled on, Balkrishna Hari meanwhile on the suspicion that the occupants of the following carriage were whispering to each other, fired at the head of one of them from behind. Lieutenant Ayerst, Rand’s military escort who was riding in the following carriage died on the spot, Rand was taken to Sassoon Hospital where he succumbed to his injuries 3 July 1897.

Khando Vishnu Sathe on a cycle on his way back to Pune city shouted at a home "गणेश खिंडीत गणपती पावला हो !" (Ganpati of Ganesh Valley has favoured us!) From the window, Lokmanya Tilak appeared, smiled and closed the window.

Context:
That year, in spite of the plague, British were adamant to conduct Matric exams of the students (10/11th equivalent.) Angered by the rude and adamant behavior of the officers, the Chapekar brothers burned the exam canopy down to ashes. The British officers used to examine the ppl, especially women, publicly by removing their cloths and molesting them. Many women were raped and molested by these officers who were appointed "Just to examine".

e22d58f953.b: Observed on Amāvāsyā tithi of Mārgaśīrṣaḥ (lunar) month (Aparāhṇaḥ/vyaapti).
e22d58f953.d:
KhechMavas or Khichdi Amavasya is a traditional winter ceremony of the Kashmiri Pandits, celebrated during Paush Krishna Paksha Amavasya (Purnimanta), locally known as Poh Gaet Pach Mavas. This festival, steeped in religious devotion, is a vital part of the Kashmiri religious and cultural heritage and symbolizes the region's history. It honors the Yakshas, who inhabit the Himalayan heights, stretching from modern-day Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh to Kashmir. According to lore, these beings from Kashmir's towering mountains and would descend to the plains during winter. The Kashmiri people would welcome them with the specialty dish Khichdi as a gesture of hospitality.

On the evening of Khichdi Amavasya, a special Khichdi is prepared using rice, turmeric powder, and pounded moong dal, embodying sanctity and purity. It is served on a fresh earthen plate (Toke), a handwoven grass base called Arie, or a thali, depending on local tradition (Reeth). Alongside, a pestle (Kaajvut) is placed upright on a grass-woven Arie, and a Tilak is applied before performing Pooja. Subsequently, a portion of the Khichdi is placed on the house's courtyard wall and later consumed as prasad.

e2d2d7d740.b: Event occured on 1446-10-20 (gregorian). Julian date was converted to Gregorian in this reckoning.
e2d2d7d740.d:
On this day, mahArANa kumbha routed Khalji alAdin Mahmud sultAn of mAlva for a third time. mahmUd was trying to invade mevAr with a large army, but was attacked while he was crossing of River Banas and chased back to maNDu.

Context
mahmUd had given refuge to the murderer of kumbha's father (about 1433). In 1439, kumbha demanded his extradition, but mahmUd refused. In the Battle of Sarangpur, kumbha attacked and made mahmUd prisoner for 6 months - but freed him for a tribute. 

In 1442, mahmUd invaded mewar to extract vengence, desecrated bana-mAtA temple, used the pieces as weights for butchers to weigh meat, and made hindus eat powder from the mUrti as pAn. kumbha routed him in the Battle of Mandalgarh.

Aftermath
Mahmud did not dare attack Mewar for the next 8 years.

Context
This came after May 13 Jaipur bombings (63 killed), 25 July bengaLUru bombings and 26 July Ahmedabad bombings (56 killed). 

Aftermath
Several people (many engineers, scrap dealer, hotlier) were arrested. Abdul Qureshi (Quraysh = Islamic prophet's tribe) aka Al Arabi, a SIMI activist with IT background was alleged to be closely involved. He was arrested after a gun fight in 2018.

e41d21748d.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°36′15.71″, 0°36′02.30″ apart, disc-to-disc. śaniḥ at rēvatī-4 mīnaḥ (latitude 2°15′32.12″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude +0.71, elongation 25°42′15.38″ W). śukraḥ at rēvatī-4 mīnaḥ (latitude 1°39′16.41″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -3.87, elongation 25°39′40.90″ W). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here śaniḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) śaniḥ is taken as jayI over śukraḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

e4493dcae0.b: Event occured on 1683-11-19 (gregorian). Julian date was converted to Gregorian in this reckoning.
e4493dcae0.d:
Maratha reinforcements, which included Sambhaji himself, arrived from Rajapur to rescue the fort with 800 cavalry and 2,000 infantry.

Portuguese viceroy thought that Sambhaji will attack him from the rear and cut his line of communication with Goa. On 10 November, the viceroy called for a general retreat towards the Durbhat port. The Marathas routed the retreating Portuguese by attacking them from a hill near creek. The viceroy was wounded during this skirmish. On 12 November most of the Portuguese army reached Goa.

Context: During the marATha-portuguese war under sambaji, the Portuguese viceroy marched towards the Fortress of Ponda, with 3,700 soldiers. They crossed the river and reached the villages west of Ponda on 7th November. Veteran Maratha general Yesaji Kank and his son Krishnaji were stationed at Ponda with a force of 600 soldiers. The Marathas resisted the initial Portuguese infantry charges. In one of these skirmishes Krishnaji Kank was wounded heavily, he died a few days later. However The Portuguese heavy bombardment managed to break through the walls of the fort, severely damaging it.

e4ab9ef175.d:
Operation Searchlight, specially targetting Bengali Hindus and nationalists, began on this day. It marked the beginning of the genocide in bangladesh as well as the Bangla war of liberation.


They put Mujibur Rahman behind bars and ambushed the Dhaka university, resulting in the death of 9 teachers and 200 students in Iqbal Hal. Similarly, the Pakistan army continued with its barbaric attacks on civilians in Old Dhaka, Tejgaon, Indira Road, Mirpur, Kalabagan and other places.

On the same night, several people in Chittagong were shot dead by army personnel. National newspapers, including, Daily Ittefaq, the Daily Sangbad were shut down and their offices were set ablaze, resulting in the death of several media personnel.

Mass graves were dug out and hastily bulldozed. An estimated 700 people were burnt to death in Dhaka. Similarly, they set fire to the houses of slum dwellers, fired bullets at those running away to save their lives, razed a Kali Mandir and also destroyed the Central Shaheed Minar.

Aftermath
It is believed that around 10,000-35,000 Bengalis were killed by the Pakistan army under Operation Searchlight. In the months to follow, Pakistani military and supporting Islamist militias from Jamaat-e-Islami (lit. Collective of Islamists) killed up to 3 million people, raped between 200k and 400k Bengali women. A further eight to ten million people, mostly Hindus, fled to India.

Of course, the operation failed and backfired, as India under Indira Gandhi intervened and utterly defeated the Islamic republic's military in 14 days. Bangladesh has tried and hanged several war criminals. Pakistan continues to dispute the 1971 genocide.

Contemporary report by Ted Kennedy: 

> "Hardest hit have been members of the Hindu community who have been robbed of their lands and shops, systematically slaughtered, and in some places, painted with yellow patches marked H. All of this has been officially sanctioned, ordered and implemented under martial law from Islamabad".

Sources
- OpIndia article.

e51d790810.b: Observed on Uttaraphalgunī nakshatra of Dhanuḥ (sidereal solar) month (Prātaḥ/paraviddha).
e51d790810.d:
Between the 6th and 9th centuries, in South India, there existed 63 ardent devotees of Bhagavan Shiva, collectively known as the Nayanmars. These devout individuals, hailing from various walks of life including potters, fishermen, farmers, merchants, priests, hunters, and washermen, created devotional songs still sung by followers around the globe. Among these Nayanmars, Appar, Sambandar, and Sundarar, known for their Thevaram hymns, along with Manikkavasagar, are distinguished as the Samayacharyas or the ‘The Four’ (nālvar) revered teachers of the faith. They were instrumental in promoting the Shaiva Siddhanta philosophy and culture, effectively challenging the spread of Jainism and Buddhism. Their teachings centered around the concept that Shiva embodies love, and that embracing love for all beings and existence is essential in connecting with Shiva, the Supreme Being.

The 3rd of the Nayanmars was Iyarpagai Nayanmar, a Vaishya and native of Kaveripoompattinam, renowned for his extraordinary charity, particularly towards devotees of Bhagavan Shiva. He had vowed never to refuse a request from a Shiva Bhakta. His devotion caught the attention of Bhagavan Shiva, who decided to test him. Disguised as a Brahmana, Bhagavan Shiva visited Nayanmar's home and, after being warmly welcomed, asked for Nayanmar's wife as a gift. Nayanmar, without hesitation or doubt, agreed to this unusual request, showcasing his unwavering devotion and belief in serving devotees.

The Nayanmar's wife, following her husband's decision and considering him as her god and law, consented to go with the Brahmana. As they left the town, Nayanmar accompanied them, armed for their protection. When the Nayanmar's in-laws learned of this event, they furiously confronted them, ready to fight to death rather than face the shame. Nayanmar, in his commitment to fulfill the Brahmana's wish, fought and killed his wife's relatives.

After reaching the temple of Tiruchaikadu, the Brahmana asked the Nayanmar to leave. As Nayanmar started to return home, he was called back by the Brahmana, only to find his wife alone and the Brahmana gone. At that moment, Bhagavan Shiva and Mother Parvati appeared, praising the couple's supreme devotion. They blessed the Nayanmar and his wife with a place in their divine abode. Nayanmar’s relatives (who earlier died at his hands) also attained the lotus feet of Bhagavan Shiva. This story illustrates the depth of unquestioning devotion and its alignment with Dharma, as well as the divine grace bestowed upon true devotees.
e51d790810.r: - 63 Nayanmar Saints by Swami Sivananda, published by The Divine Life Society

e58c865a81.d:
On this day died shrI-kRShNadeva-rAya, who ruled vijayanagara at its peak.

An inscription in Honehalli near Tumkur records this. Saka 1451 Virodhi Kartika Shuddha Pournima, lunar eclipse.

e5ab612939.b: Event occured on 1710-05-23 (gregorian). Julian date was converted to Gregorian in this reckoning.
e5ab612939.d:
Banda Bahadur, the vaiShNava disciple of Guru Gobind, crushed a mogol army. The Mughals were armed with artillery, well equipped cavalry and large infantry whereas the Sikhs had cavalry and infantry but no artillery. In the battle, his Sikhs gave a crushing blow to the Mughal empire. Wazir Khan (Sirhind) was killed in the battle and Sikhs established their first Raj in Punjab.

The bandai khAlsa was heavily hinduised (eg. vegetarianism, red dress).

e5c0448165.b: Observed on Śukla-Pañcamī tithi of Māghaḥ (lunar) month (Madhyāhnaḥ/puurvaviddha).
e5c0448165.d: Māgha Shukla Panchami is considered as Shri Panchami or Vasanta Panchami.  In Northern Bharat, pūjā of Lakshmi Devi sameta Mahavishnu, Rati Devī sameta Kāma Deva, and Vasanta Deva is performed on this day. A great utsava is done wearing new clothes, playing instruments and singing in Vasanta Raga. Such traditions are recorded in compilations such as Vrata Rāja, Jayasimha Kalpa Druma, Nirnaya Sindhu etc. It is important to pray to Bhagavan to give us the happiness to celebrate life, and the prosperity and physical vigour needed to take Dharma forward including begetting Dharmic progeny.
e5c0448165.s:

𑌮𑍌𑌲𑍌 𑌗𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌾-𑌶𑌶𑌾𑌙𑍍𑌕𑍌 𑌕𑌰𑌚𑌰𑌣𑌤𑌲𑍇 𑌶𑍀𑌤𑌲𑌾𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌾 𑌭𑍁𑌜𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌾𑌃  
𑌵𑌾𑌮𑍇 𑌭𑌾𑌗𑍇 𑌦𑌯𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌾 𑌹𑌿𑌮𑌗𑌿𑌰𑌿𑌦𑍁𑌹𑌿𑌤𑌾 𑌚𑌨𑍍𑌦𑌨𑌂 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌗𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍇।  
𑌇𑌤𑍍𑌥𑌂 𑌶𑍀𑌤𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌭𑍂𑌤𑌂 𑌤𑌵 𑌕𑌨𑌕𑌸𑌭𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌥 𑌸𑍋𑌢𑍁𑌂 𑌕𑍍𑌵 𑌶𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌃

e60299c8dd.b: Observed on Śukla-Daśamī tithi of Bhādrapadaḥ (lunar) month (Sūryōdayaḥ/puurvaviddha).
e60299c8dd.d: On this daśamī day of the bright fortnight of Nabhasya (Bhadrapada), the Dashavatara Vratam is observed. After Snanam, Sandhya, Deva-rishi-pitr-tarpanam etc., one should worship the ten avataras (of Vishnu), viz. Matsya, Kurma, Varaha, Narasimha, Trivikrama, Parshurama, Shri Rama, Krishna, Buddha and Kalki. One should worship ten golden images (pratimā) of these incarnations and donate them to ten Brahmanas. One should fast or eat once and should also feed the Brahmanas. Having performed this vratam with devotion, one ultimately goes to the eternal viṣṇulōka, in a vimānam.
e60299c8dd.s:
𑌅𑌥𑍋 𑌨𑌭𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌶𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌦𑌶𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌜𑌸𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌮।  
𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌂 𑌦𑌶𑌾𑌵𑌤𑌾𑌰𑌾𑌖𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌜𑌲𑌾𑌶𑌯𑍇॥௧௪॥  
𑌕𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌸𑌨𑍍𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌿𑌯𑌮𑌂 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌷𑌿𑌪𑌿𑌤𑍃𑌤𑌰𑍍𑌪𑌣𑌮𑍍।  
𑌤𑌤𑍋 𑌦𑌶𑌾𑌵𑌤𑌾𑌰𑌾𑌣𑌿 𑌸𑌮𑌭𑍍𑌯𑌰𑍍𑌚𑍇𑌤𑍍 𑌸𑌮𑌾𑌹𑌿𑌤𑌃॥௧௫॥  
𑌮𑌤𑍍𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌕𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌂 𑌵𑌰𑌾𑌹𑌂 𑌚 𑌨𑌰𑌸𑌿𑌂𑌹𑌂 𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌵𑌿𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌮𑌮𑍍।  
𑌰𑌾𑌮𑌂 𑌰𑌾𑌮𑌂 𑌚 𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌂 𑌚 𑌬𑍌𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌂 𑌕𑌲𑍍𑌕𑌿𑌨𑌮𑍇𑌵 𑌚॥௧௬॥  
𑌦𑌶𑌮𑍃𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌸𑍌𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌣𑍀𑌃 𑌪𑍂𑌜𑌯𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌵𑌿𑌧𑌾𑌨𑌤𑌃।  
𑌦𑌶𑌭𑍍𑌯𑍋 𑌵𑌿𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌯𑍇𑌭𑍍𑌯𑍋 𑌦𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌸𑌤𑍍𑌕𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌯 𑌨𑌾𑌰𑌦॥௧௭॥  
𑌉𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌂 𑌚𑍇𑌕𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌂 𑌕𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌭𑍋𑌜𑍍𑌯 𑌵𑌾𑌡𑌵𑌾𑌨𑍍।  
𑌵𑌿𑌸𑍃𑌜𑍍𑌯 𑌪𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌾𑌦𑍍 𑌭𑍁𑌞𑍍𑌜𑍀𑌤 𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌯𑌂 𑌸𑍍𑌵𑍇𑌷𑍍𑌟𑍈𑌃 𑌸𑌮𑌾𑌹𑌿𑌤𑌃॥௧௮॥  
𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌕𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌂 𑌤𑍍𑌵𑍇𑌤𑌦𑍍𑌭𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌭𑍋𑌗𑌾𑌨𑌿𑌹𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌮𑌾𑌨𑍍।  
𑌵𑌿𑌮𑌾𑌨𑍇𑌨 𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌜𑍇𑌦𑍍 𑌅𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌲𑍋𑌕𑌂 𑌸𑌨𑌾𑌤𑌨𑌮𑍍॥௧௯॥

e608c42b4b.d: Special vrata day for Ganesha. In this month, Ganesha is worshipped as bhālachandra-mahāgaṇapatiḥ. Fast during the day and pray to Ganesha after moonrise, chanting the shloka mentioned.
e608c42b4b.s:
𑌗𑌣𑌾𑌧𑌿𑌪𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌂 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑍇𑌶 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌥𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌪𑍂𑌜𑌿𑌤𑍋 𑌮𑌯𑌾।  
𑌕𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌂 𑌮𑍋𑌚𑌯𑍇𑌶𑌾𑌨 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌮𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌂 𑌚 𑌦𑍇𑌹𑌿 𑌮𑍇॥  
  
𑌯𑌦𑌾 𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌲𑍇𑌶𑌿𑌤𑍋 𑌮𑌰𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑍋 𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌦𑍁𑌃𑌖𑍈𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌦𑌾𑌰𑍁𑌣𑍈𑌃।  
𑌤𑌦𑌾 𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍇 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌥𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌵𑍈 𑌪𑍂𑌜𑌨𑍀𑌯𑍋 𑌗𑌣𑌾𑌧𑌿𑌪𑌃॥ (𑌭𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑌮𑍍)

e61f11b1cc.b: Observed on Kr̥ṣṇa-Caturdaśī tithi of every (lunar) month (Sāṅgavaḥ/paraviddha).
e61f11b1cc.d: Anadhyayana on account of chaturdaśī. Several tithis in a month are nitya-anadhyayana days, including prathamā, aṣṭamī, chaturdaśī, amāvāsyā and pūrṇimā. Manu has said that performing adhyayana on these days destroys the Guru (Amavasya), Shishya (Chaturdashi) and the vīrya of the brahma (vēda) itself (Ashtami/Purnima). Similarly, Jabali Rishi has said that Adhyayana on prathama hurts the buddhi while adhyayana on chaturdaśī hurts the brahma (vēda) itself!
e61f11b1cc.s:
𑌹𑌾𑌰𑍀𑌤𑌃—  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌿𑌪𑌤𑍍𑌸𑍁 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌪𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌣𑍋𑌰𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌯𑍋𑌃।  
𑌶𑍍𑌵𑍋𑌽𑌨𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑍇𑌽𑌦𑍍𑌯 𑌶𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌨𑌾𑌧𑍀𑌯𑍀𑌤 𑌕𑌦𑌾𑌚𑌨॥  
𑌮𑌨𑍁𑌃—  
𑌅𑌮𑌾𑌵𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌗𑍁𑌰𑍁𑌂 𑌹𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌶𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌹𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌦𑌶𑍀।  
𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑌾𑌪𑍌𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌮𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑌰𑌿𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌜𑌯𑍇𑌦𑌿𑌤𑌿॥  
𑌯𑌾𑌜𑍍𑌞𑌵𑌲𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌯𑌃—  
𑌪𑌞𑍍𑌚𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌅𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍁𑌸𑍂𑌤𑌕𑍇।  
𑌜𑌾𑌬𑌾𑌲𑌿𑌃—  
𑌨𑌾𑌧𑍀𑌯𑍀𑌤 𑌨𑌰𑍋 𑌨𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌮𑌾𑌦𑌾𑌵𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌚 𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌯𑍋𑌃।  
𑌆𑌦𑍌 𑌚 𑌹𑍀𑌯𑌤𑍇 𑌬𑍁𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌿𑌰𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌚 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮 𑌹𑍀𑌯𑌤𑍇॥  
𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌿𑌪𑌤𑍍, 𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌃 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌦𑌶𑍀॥

e647559efe.b: Event occured on 1680-03-03 (gregorian). Julian date was converted to Gregorian in this reckoning.
e647559efe.d:
On 22 February, the Emperor Aurangzeb, waging a war against udayapura, went to look at Chitor, and by his order the 63 temples of the place were destroyed.

Context
After the death of Maharaja Jaswant Singh of Jodhpur in the Kabul Subah, he tried to eliminate the Rathors of Marwar as a political power in Rajputana. But Maharana Raj Singh of Mewar, in line with the great traditions of his House, came out in open support of the Rathors.. This led to war with both Mewar and Marwar during which the temples built on the bank of Rana’s lake were destroyed by his orders. 

Raj Singh opposed Aurangzeb multiple times, once to save the Kishangarh princess Charumati from the Mughals and once by denouncing the Jizya tax levied by Aurangzeb. Chatrapati Shivaji Maharaj had once taunted Aurangzeb by telling him to ask the Rana of Mewar who is the head of the Hindus for Jizya if he had the guts instead of terrorising unarmed citizens.

e6598d794f.b: Observed on Kr̥ṣṇa-Caturdaśī tithi of Āśvayujaḥ (lunar) month (Sūryōdayaḥ/puurvaviddha).
e6598d794f.d: Perform Deepa Danam for Yamadharmaraja in evening
e6598d794f.s:
𑌜𑍍𑌯𑍋𑌤𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌨𑌿𑌬𑌨𑍍𑌧𑍇---  
𑌤𑍁𑌲𑌾𑌸𑌂𑌸𑍍𑌥𑍇 𑌸𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌂𑌶𑍌 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌦𑍋𑌷𑍇 𑌭𑍂𑌤𑌦𑌰𑍍𑌶𑌯𑍋𑌃।  
𑌉𑌲𑍍𑌕𑌾𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌾 𑌨𑌰𑌾𑌃 𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌃 𑌪𑌿𑌤𑍄𑌣𑌾𑌂 𑌮𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌗𑌦𑌰𑍍𑌶𑌨𑌮𑍍॥  
𑌉𑌲𑍍𑌕𑌾𑌗𑍍𑌰𑌹𑌣𑌤𑌦𑍍𑌦𑌾𑌨𑌵𑌿𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌜𑌨𑍇𑌷𑍁 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌃---  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌚𑍍𑌯𑌨𑌿𑌬𑌨𑍍𑌧𑍇---  
𑌶𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌶𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌹𑌤𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌂 𑌚 𑌭𑍂𑌤𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌂 𑌭𑍂𑌤𑌦𑌰𑍍𑌶𑌯𑍋𑌃।  
𑌉𑌜𑍍𑌜𑍍𑌵𑌲𑌜𑍍𑌯𑍋𑌤𑌿𑌷𑌾 𑌦𑍇𑌹𑌂 𑌦𑌹𑍇𑌯𑌂 𑌵𑍍𑌯𑍋𑌮𑌵𑌹𑍍𑌨𑌿𑌨𑌾॥  
𑌅𑌗𑍍𑌨𑌿𑌦𑌗𑍍𑌧𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌯𑍇 𑌜𑍀𑌵𑌾 𑌯𑍇𑌽𑌪𑍍𑌯𑌦𑌗𑍍𑌧𑌾𑌃 𑌕𑍁𑌲𑍇 𑌮𑌮।  
𑌉𑌜𑍍𑌜𑍍𑌵𑌲𑌜𑍍𑌯𑍋𑌤𑌿𑌷𑌾 𑌦𑌗𑍍𑌧𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌯𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌪𑌰𑌮𑌾𑌂 𑌗𑌤𑌿𑌮𑍍॥  
𑌯𑌮𑌲𑍋𑌕𑌂 𑌪𑌰𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌜𑍍𑌯 𑌆𑌗𑌤𑌾 𑌯𑍇 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌪𑌥𑍇।  
𑌉𑌜𑍍𑌜𑍍𑌵𑌲𑌜𑍍𑌯𑍋𑌤𑌿𑌷𑌾 𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌮 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌪𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍋 𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌜𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌤𑍇॥  
𑌲𑍈𑌙𑍍𑌗𑍇---  
𑌤𑌤𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌤𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌭𑍋𑌜𑌯𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌤𑌪𑍋𑌧𑌨𑌾𑌨𑍍।  
𑌶𑍈𑌵𑌾𑌨𑍍 𑌵𑌿𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌂𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌥 𑌪𑌰𑌾𑌨𑍍 𑌶𑌿𑌵𑌲𑍋𑌕𑍇 𑌮𑌹𑍀𑌯𑌤𑍇।  
𑌦𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌤𑍁 𑌤𑍇𑌭𑍍𑌯𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌯𑌮𑌲𑍋𑌕𑌂 𑌨 𑌗𑌚𑍍𑌛𑌤𑌿॥  
𑌮𑌾𑌷𑌪𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌶𑌾𑌕𑍇𑌨 𑌭𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌦𑌿𑌨𑍇 𑌨𑌰𑌃।  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌤𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌦𑌶𑍀𑌕𑌾𑌲𑍇 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌪𑌾𑌪𑍈𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌮𑍁𑌚𑍍𑌯𑌤𑍇॥

e6708be523.s:
𑌸𑍇𑌨𑌾𑌵𑌿𑌦𑌾𑌰𑌕 𑌸𑍍𑌕𑌨𑍍𑌦 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌸𑍇𑌨 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌬𑌲।  
𑌰𑍁𑌦𑍍𑌰𑍋𑌮𑌾𑌗𑍍𑌨𑌿𑌜 𑌷𑌡𑍍𑌵𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌗𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌾𑌗𑌰𑍍𑌭 𑌨𑌮𑍋𑌽𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌤𑍇॥

e67802a78d.b: Observed on Kr̥ṣṇa-Prathamā tithi of Māghaḥ (lunar) month (Aparāhṇaḥ/vyaapti). The event occurred in 4486 (Kali era).
e67802a78d.d: Sarvajñaviṣṇu (name of Śrī Vidyātīrtha before initiation), son of Śārṅgapāṇi) of Bilvāraṇya received initiation into asceticism from the sage preceptor Chandraśekhara; remaining in the seat of the master, engrossed in/attached to the worship of Bhagavan Yogeśa and the Devī who dwells in the Chakrarāja, He was surrounded by the eminent saints—Śrī Mādhava, Bukka and Bhārati tīrtha. He decorated the seat by remaining in Kāṅci only for seventy-three years and after directing eight disciples who shone like the presiding deities of eight quarters to take care of the Pīṭha, He, the steadfast one, resorting to the peaks of Himalayas with the only companion disciple, Śaṅkarānanda, observed severe penance for fifteen years. This preceptor, in the course of penance itself, as the attending disciple was looking at, merged in the Supreme Effulgence of the Sun on the pratipad (first day) of the dark fortnight of the Māgha month in the year Raktākṣī. The disciple too afflicted with grief heavily returned to his Maṭha. In the meantime, the eight disciples too protected the Pīṭha as per the directions; gladdened on seeing the disciple Śaṅkarānanda, they entered into that Maṭha of their preceptor. This preceptor, adored by Śrī Vidyāraṇya, Saccidānanda and others is also known popularly as Vidyānātha, Vidyeśa, Vidyāśaṅkara, Vidyātīrtha and Śaṅkarānandaguru.
e67802a78d.s:
𑌬𑌿𑌲𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌰𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌜𑌶𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌪𑌾𑌣𑌿𑌤𑌨𑌯𑌃 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌜𑍍𑌞𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌃 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌯𑌨𑍍  
𑌸𑌨𑍍𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌸𑌂 𑌗𑍁𑌰𑍁𑌚𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌶𑍇𑌖𑌰𑌮𑍁𑌨𑍇𑌰𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌥𑌾𑌯 𑌪𑍀𑌠𑍀𑌂 𑌗𑍁𑌰𑍋𑌃  
𑌯𑍋𑌗𑍇𑌶𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌚 𑌚𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌰𑌾𑌜𑌵𑌸𑌤𑍇𑌰𑍍𑌦𑍇𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌸𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍋𑌽𑌰𑍍𑌚𑌨𑍇  
𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌧𑌵𑌬𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌕𑌭𑌾𑌰𑌤𑌿𑌯𑌤𑌿𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌷𑍍𑌠𑍈𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌹𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌠𑍈𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍃𑌤𑌃॥௯௮॥  
𑌕𑌾𑌞𑍍𑌚𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑍇𑌵 𑌸 𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌤𑌿𑌂 𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌸𑌹𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌂 𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌷𑌾𑌨𑍍 𑌵𑌿𑌭𑍂𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌸𑌨𑌂  
𑌶𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌨𑌷𑍍𑌟 𑌦𑌿𑌶𑌾𑌗𑌜𑌾𑌯𑌿𑌤𑌯𑌤𑍀𑌨𑍍 𑌆𑌦𑌿𑌶𑍍𑌯 𑌪𑍀𑌠𑌾𑌵𑌨𑍇।  
𑌯𑌾𑌵𑌤𑍍𑌪𑌞𑍍𑌚𑌦𑌶𑌾𑌬𑍍𑌦𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌹𑌿𑌮𑌵𑌚𑍍𑌛𑍃𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌯𑌃 𑌶𑌙𑍍𑌕𑌰𑌾-  
𑌨𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍈𑌕𑌾𑌨𑍁𑌚𑌰𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌚𑌾𑌰 𑌪𑌰𑌮𑌂 𑌧𑍀𑌰𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌪𑍋 𑌦𑍁𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌰𑌮𑍍॥௯௯॥  
𑌤𑌪𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌨𑍇𑌵𑌾𑌸𑍌 𑌤𑌰𑍁𑌣𑌤𑌰𑌣𑍇𑌰𑍍𑌧𑌾𑌮𑍍𑌨𑌿 𑌪𑌰𑌮𑍇  
𑌨𑌿𑌲𑍀𑌨𑍋𑌽𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌰𑍍𑌹𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌨𑌿𑌮𑌿𑌷𑌤𑌿 𑌚 𑌪𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌶𑍍𑌵𑍇 𑌪𑌰𑌿𑌚𑌰𑍇।  
𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌤𑍋 𑌰𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌬𑍍𑌦𑍇 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌿𑌪𑌦𑌿 𑌤𑌪𑌸𑍍𑌯𑍇𑌷 𑌬𑌹𑍁𑌲𑍇  
𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌸𑌨𑍍 𑌶𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌯𑍋𑌽𑌪𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌵𑍃𑌤𑌦𑍍 𑌅𑌸𑌦𑌤𑍍 𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌂 𑌚 𑌸 𑌮𑌠𑌮𑍍॥௧௦௦॥  
𑌅𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌰𑍇𑌽𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌾𑌪𑌿 𑌯𑌥𑌾𑌨𑌿𑌯𑍋𑌗𑌮𑍍 𑌆𑌚𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌪𑍀𑌠𑍀𑌮𑍍 𑌅𑌵𑌿𑌰𑍋𑌧𑌮𑌾𑌵𑍁𑌃।  
𑌤𑌂 𑌶𑌙𑍍𑌕𑌰𑌾𑌨𑌨𑍍𑌦𑌮𑍍 𑌉𑌦𑍀𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌯 𑌹𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌾𑌃 𑌦𑍇𑌷𑍍𑌟𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌠𑌂 𑌤𑌂 𑌨𑌿𑌰𑌵𑍀𑌵𑌿𑌶𑌨𑍍𑌤॥௧௦௧॥  
—𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌶𑍍𑌲𑍋𑌕𑌮𑌞𑍍𑌜𑌰𑍀

e6846691a0.d: Budhaḥ sets into combustion (astamayaH), heading prāk (east), on 2027-Nov-18 20:51. At this moment budhaḥ is at svātī-4 tulā (latitude 1°23′22.64″ N, moving r̥ju (direct)), magnitude -0.84, elongation 13°09′00.50″ W of the Sun. e6ae2a4188.d: Budhaḥ rises out of combustion (udayaH), heading prāk (east), on 2026-Jul-21 08:18. At this moment budhaḥ is at punarvasuḥ-1 mithunam (latitude 4°31′39.54″ S, moving vakra (retrograde)), magnitude +2.82, elongation 12°32′28.91″ W of the Sun. Emergence from combustion restores a graha's full strength; this is generally considered an auspicious time to begin activities connected with budhaḥ's significations.

e6b851e784.d:
On this day, shortly before his untimely death, one of the finest peshva-s, mAdhava rAv issued his final will with the following points.

- 1. All my debts should be paid even by using, if necessary, my private purse  in the possession of Guruji (Mahadaji Ballal) :
- 2. The system of farming the revenues is found oppressive to the ryots: it should be modified after a careful enquiry.
- 3. The two holy places Prayag and Benares should be released from Muslim control. This was the ardent desire of my sires and now is the time to carry it out.
- 4. My mother's desire to perform the pilgrimage of Benares should be fulfilled as soon as convenient.
- 5. The obsequies of Bhau Saheb should be performed next February, whether aunt Parwatibai becomes sati or not.
- 6. The annuities assigned to the worthy Brahmans of Benares should be regularly paid and continued in heredity.
- 7. Dinners in connection with my funeral rites should be served to two lacs of Brahmans each with half an anna for dakshana.
- 8. Dadasaheb should have five lacs of jagir assigned for his maintenance in order to keep him contented.
- 9. The charities of the Shravan month should be continued as long as the administration brings in at least 5 lacs of revenue yearly.

The responsible officers swore in the presence of Ganapati that they would execute all these wishes.

e6c7815b31.d: Raju Sastrigal, or Brahmashri Tyāgarāja Makhi, popularly known as ‘Mannargudi Periyava’, was a revered scholar and a significant figure in the early 19th to early 20th century in Tamil Nadu. He was a grihastha (householder), not a sannyasi, which made it remarkable that he was addressed as ‘Periyava’ - in the words of the 68th Shankaracharya of the Kanchi Kamakoti Peetham, Shri Chandrashekharendra Sarasvati Swamigal. He hailed from the same clan as Appayya Dikshita, a prominent 16th-century Advaita scholar. Mannargudi Periyava was renowned as a scholar of repute, a great Śiva bhakta, and for his exemplary adherence to anushthanas. He ran a gurukulam (traditional school) where he trained numerous scholars (vidvāns), with even sanyasis learning from him, earning him the title of ‘Kulapati’. In 1887, during Queen Victoria’s Golden Jubilee, the British Government awarded him the title of ‘Maha Mahopadhyaya’ for his scholarship. He initially declined it out of humility, believing he did not deserve a title previously awarded to very great vidvāns. The award was eventually sent to his home by the District Collector. He was known for his dignified approach to scholarly debates. When a contemporary, Ramasubba Sastrigal, attacked Advaita, Sannyasam, and Shiva bhakti, Mannargudi Periyava countered his arguments in a book titled Durjanokti-nirasam without using any offensive language. His work Nyayendu Shekharam is a notable treatise that combines Vedanta and Tarka shastra (the science of logic and reasoning), often referred to as Nyaya Shastram. He wrote Nyayendu Shekharam to refute Nyaya Bhaskaram by Anantharyar, which had criticized Advaita. He named his work ‘Nyayendu’ (moon) to symbolize its ability to “cool the hearts” after the “sun” (Bhaskaram). In his humility, he considered the book to be a divine gift (Ishvara prasad), hence he chose ‘Indhu Shekhara’ (meaning ‘moon’ and associated with Ishvara) to be part of its title. Nyayendu Shekharam holds such importance that it is used for annual examinations by the Advaita Sabha of Kumbhaghonam, an institution established by the Paramaguru Swamigal (the 6th Chandrashekharendra Sarasvati, and the 65th Shankaracharya of the Kanchi Kamakoti Peetham) in 1894. He integrated a Pillaiyar Sruthi (hymn) into Nyayendu Shekharam, connecting Pillaiyar (Vinayaka) to Tarka Shastram. This hymn states that even those who worship other deities first offer prayers to Vigneshvara to remove obstacles.

e6d088aa92.d: Anadhyayana on account of manvādi. On the days of Ayana (solstices), Vishu (equinoxes), the day when Bhagavan Vishnu goes to sleep (Shayana Ekadashi) or awakens (Utthana Ekadashi) as well as the Manvadi and Yugadi days, one is not supposed to perform Adhyayana.

e6d5f4aa81.d:
On this day, after Direct action day killing of Hindus began, Gopal Chandra Mukhopadhyay aka Gopal Patha (a mutton shop keeper) began retaliating against Islamists.

> Gopal Patha had already founded the Bharat Jatiya Bahini, an organisation of young men to help fellow citizens during a natural calamity. On the 17th, Gopal Patha turned from a philanthropist to a warrior, ready to defend his people. Throughout the night, Gopal Patha, along with his young men from the Bharat Jayati Bahini worked on a plan on how they could defend Hindus from the Muslim barbarians.  
> The marwaris offered finances, others spent the night making weapons for them. Muslim League chief minister of Bengal, Huseyn Shaheed Suhrawardy and the Muslim League goons had decided on the 17th that they were going to take two more days to complete the annihilation of Hindus.  
> But they had not taken into consideration their greatest roadblock – Gopal Patha. From the 18th to 20th, Gopal Patha and his men put up a brave fight, paying the Muslim League goons back in equal measure, if not more.  
> Historian Sandip Bandopadhyay wrote, “They faced resistance everywhere. Hindu youths counter-attacked with such ferocity that the Muslim League men had to flee. Many were killed. Emboldened by their success in taking on and defeating their Islamist attackers, Hindu youths took the fight to Muslim-majority areas and started killing Islamist men. They did not, however, touch Muslim women and children or the aged and the infirm”.  
> By the 19th of August, suddenly, the Muslims started feeling unsafe. Only two days of retribution, of self-defence, and the Muslim League started running with tail between their legs.  
> It was only on the 21st of August when the Muslims had started feeling unsafe because the Hindus dared to defend themselves, did Viceroy’s rule come into action in Bengal.  
> From an OpIndia article

e70695178a.s:
𑌯𑌃 𑌮𑌾𑌧𑌵𑍇 𑌵𑍈𑌶𑌾𑌖𑌮𑌾𑌸𑍇, 𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍋𑌦𑌶𑍀𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌦𑌶𑍀𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌿𑌮𑌾𑌸𑍁 𑌤𑌿𑌥𑌿𑌷𑍁 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌕𑌂 𑌕𑌰𑍋𑌤𑌿  
𑌸 𑌨𑌿𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌯𑍇𑌨 𑌮𑍋𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌨𑍁𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍। 𑌯𑌥𑌾 𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾 𑌧𑌨𑌶𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌾 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌣𑌃 𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌤𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌚  
𑌮𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌿𑌤𑌿। 𑌅𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌸𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌾 𑌕𑌥𑌾 𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌦𑌶𑌾𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌮𑌕𑌪𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌮𑍋𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌵𑍈𑌶𑌾𑌖𑌮𑌾𑌹𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌮𑍍𑌯𑍇।  
𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾 𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌨𑌾 𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍋𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌹𑌿𑌰𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌃, 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌮𑌧𑍁𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌘𑌾𑌤𑌿𑌤𑌃,  
𑌪𑍌𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌮𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌭𑍂𑌮𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌾𑌰𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌕𑍃𑌤𑌃, 𑌤𑌤𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌭𑍃𑌤𑌿 𑌤𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌥𑌯𑌃 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌜𑌾𑌤𑌾𑌃!  
𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍁𑌤𑌦𑍇𑌵 𑌉𑌵𑌾𑌚---  
𑌯𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌥𑌯𑌃 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌅𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌮𑌾𑌃 𑌶𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌕𑍇।  
𑌵𑍈𑌶𑌾𑌖𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌿 𑌰𑌾𑌜𑍇𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌿𑌮𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌃 𑌶𑍁𑌭𑌾𑌵𑌹𑌾𑌃॥௧॥  
𑌅𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌕𑌰𑌿𑌣𑍀𑌸𑌂𑌜𑍍𑌞𑌾𑌃 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌪𑌾𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌯𑌾𑌵𑌹𑌾𑌃।  
𑌮𑌾𑌧𑌵𑍇 𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌿 𑌯𑌃 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌂 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌤𑍁𑌂 𑌨 𑌚 𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌮𑌃॥௨॥  
𑌤𑌿𑌥𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌵𑍇𑌤𑌾𑌸𑍁 𑌸 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌮𑍇𑌵 𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌲𑌭𑍇𑌤𑍍।  
𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍇 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍋𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑍍𑌥𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌜𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍂𑌨𑍍𑌪𑍁𑌨𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌹𑌿॥௩॥  
𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌤𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌥𑍈𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌨𑌾 𑌸𑌹 𑌸𑌂𑌸𑍍𑌥𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌃।  
𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑌯𑌜𑍍𑌞𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌾 𑌏𑌤𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌪𑍁𑌨𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌹𑌿॥௪॥  
𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌘𑍍𑌨𑌂 𑌵𑌾 𑌸𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌪𑌂 𑌵𑌾 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌨𑍇𑌤𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌪𑍁𑌨𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌹𑌿।  
𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾 𑌜𑌜𑍍𑌞𑍇 𑌵𑍈𑌶𑌾𑌖𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑌮𑍃𑌤𑌂 𑌶𑍁𑌭𑌮𑍍॥௫॥  
𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌪𑌾𑌲𑌿𑌤𑌂 𑌤𑌚𑍍𑌚 𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌨𑌾 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌭𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌨𑌾।  
𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍋𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑍁𑌧𑌾𑌂 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌪𑌾𑌯𑌯𑌾𑌮𑌾𑌸 𑌵𑍈 𑌹𑌰𑌿𑌃॥௬॥  
𑌜𑌘𑌾𑌨 𑌚 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌦𑍈𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌵𑌿𑌰𑍋𑌧𑌿𑌨𑌃।  
𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑌾𑌮𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌜𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌬𑌭𑍂𑌵 𑌹॥௭॥  
𑌤𑌤𑍋 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌾𑌃 𑌸𑍁𑌸𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌾 𑌏𑌤𑌾𑌸𑌾𑌂 𑌚 𑌵𑌰𑌂 𑌦𑌦𑍁𑌃।  
𑌤𑌿𑌸𑍃𑌣𑌾𑌂 𑌚 𑌤𑌿𑌥𑍀𑌨𑌾𑌂 𑌵𑍈 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌤𑍍𑌯𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌫𑍁𑌲𑍍𑌲𑌵𑌿𑌲𑍋𑌚𑌨𑌾𑌃॥௮॥  
𑌏𑌤𑌾 𑌵𑍈𑌶𑌾𑌖𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌤𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌤𑌿𑌥𑌯𑌃 𑌶𑍁𑌭𑌾𑌃।  
𑌪𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌪𑍌𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌫𑌲𑌦𑌾 𑌨𑌰𑌾𑌣𑌾𑌂 𑌪𑌾𑌪𑌹𑌾𑌨𑌿𑌦𑌾𑌃॥௯॥  
𑌯𑍋𑌽𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌸𑍇 𑌚 𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑍇 𑌨 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍋 𑌮𑌨𑍁𑌜𑌾𑌧𑌮𑌃।  
𑌤𑌿𑌥𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍇 𑌤𑍁 𑌸 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌮𑍇𑌵 𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌲𑌭𑍇𑌤𑍍॥௧௦॥  
𑌤𑌿𑌥𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍇𑌽𑌪𑍍𑌯𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌣𑌃 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌦𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌕𑌂 𑌨𑌰𑌃।  
𑌚𑌾𑌣𑍍𑌡𑌾𑌲𑍀𑌂 𑌯𑍋𑌨𑌿𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌯 𑌪𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌰𑍌𑌰𑌵𑌮𑌶𑍍𑌨𑍁𑌤𑍇॥௧௧॥  
𑌉𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍋𑌦𑌕𑍇𑌨 𑌯𑌃 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌤𑌿 𑌮𑌾𑌧𑌵𑍇 𑌚 𑌤𑌿𑌥𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍇।  
𑌰𑍌𑌰𑌵𑌂 𑌨𑌰𑌕𑌂 𑌯𑌾𑌤𑌿 𑌯𑌾𑌵𑌦𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌦𑌶॥௧௨॥  
𑌪𑌿𑌤𑍄𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌸𑌮𑍁𑌦𑍍𑌦𑌿𑌶𑍍𑌯 𑌦𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌨𑌂 𑌨 𑌦𑌦𑌾𑌤𑌿 𑌯𑌃।  
𑌪𑍈𑌶𑌾𑌚𑍀𑌂 𑌯𑍋𑌨𑌿𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌯 𑌤𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌠𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌭𑍂𑌤𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌪𑍍𑌲𑌵𑌮𑍍॥௧௩॥  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌵𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌂 𑌚 𑌕𑌾𑌮𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌂 𑌮𑌾𑌧𑌵𑍇 𑌨𑌿𑌯𑌮𑍇 𑌕𑍃𑌤𑍇।  
𑌅𑌵𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌸𑌾𑌯𑍁𑌜𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌯𑍁𑌜𑍍𑌯𑌤𑍇 𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌸𑌂𑌶𑌯𑌃॥௧௪॥  
𑌆𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌂 𑌨𑌿𑌯𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌃 𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌦𑌿 𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍇।  
𑌤𑍇𑌨 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌯 𑌮𑍋𑌦𑌤𑍇 𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌦𑌿𑌰𑍇॥௧௫॥  
𑌯𑍋 𑌵𑍈 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌪𑌿𑌤𑍄𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌂 𑌗𑍁𑌰𑍁𑌮𑍁𑌦𑍍𑌦𑌿𑌶𑍍𑌯 𑌮𑌾𑌨𑌵𑌃।  
𑌨 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌦𑌿 𑌕𑌰𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌾𑌽𑌮𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌯 𑌶𑌾𑌪𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌦𑌾 𑌵𑌯𑌮𑍍॥௧௬॥  
𑌨𑌿𑌃𑌸𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌨𑍋 𑌨𑌿𑌰𑌾𑌯𑍁𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌨𑌿𑌃𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌕𑍋 𑌭𑌵𑍇𑌦𑌿𑌤𑌿।  
𑌇𑌤𑌿 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌾 𑌵𑌰𑌂 𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌧𑌾𑌮𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌯𑌯𑍁𑌃 𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾॥௧௭॥  
𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌥𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑌂 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌘𑍌𑌘𑌵𑌿𑌨𑌾𑌶𑌨𑌮𑍍।  
𑌅𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌪𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌕𑌰𑌿𑌣𑍀𑌸𑌂𑌜𑍍𑌞𑌂 𑌪𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌪𑍌𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌵𑌿𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌧𑌨𑌮𑍍॥௧௮॥  
𑌯𑌾 𑌨𑌾𑌰𑍀 𑌸𑍁𑌭𑌗𑌾𑌽𑌪𑍂𑌪𑌪𑌾𑌯𑌸𑌂 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌿𑌮𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌨𑍇।  
𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌣𑌾𑌯 𑌸𑌕𑍃𑌦𑍍𑌦𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌕𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌂 𑌸𑍁𑌤𑌂 𑌲𑌭𑍇𑌤𑍍॥௧௯॥  
𑌗𑍀𑌤𑌾𑌪𑌾𑌠𑌂 𑌤𑍁 𑌯𑌃 𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌮𑍇 𑌚 𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍇।  
𑌦𑌿𑌨𑍇𑌦𑌿𑌨𑍇𑌽𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌮𑍇𑌧𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌂 𑌫𑌲𑌮𑍇𑌤𑌿 𑌨 𑌸𑌂𑌶𑌯𑌃॥௨௦॥  
𑌸𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌨𑌾𑌮𑌪𑌠𑌨𑌂 𑌯𑌃 𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌯𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌚𑍍𑌚 𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍇।  
𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌵𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍁𑌂 𑌕𑌃 𑌶𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍋 𑌦𑌿𑌵𑌿 𑌵𑌾 𑌭𑍁𑌵𑌿॥௨௧॥  
𑌸𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌨𑌾𑌮𑌭𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌂 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌮𑌧𑍁𑌸𑍂𑌦𑌨𑌮𑍍।  
𑌪𑌯𑌸𑌾 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌯 𑌵𑍈 𑌯𑌾𑌤𑌿 𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌲𑍋𑌕𑌮𑌕𑌲𑍍𑌮𑌷𑌮𑍍॥௨௨॥  
𑌸𑌮𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌵𑌿𑌭𑌵𑍈𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌪𑍂𑌜𑌯𑍇𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌧𑍁𑌸𑍂𑌦𑌨𑌮𑍍।  
𑌨 𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌲𑍋𑌕𑌾𑌃 𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍀𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌯𑍁𑌗 𑌕𑌲𑍍𑌪𑌾𑌦𑌿 𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌯𑍇॥௨௩॥  
𑌅𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌚𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌯𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌚 𑌵𑍈𑌶𑌾𑌖𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌮𑌤𑍋 𑌯𑌦𑌿।  
𑌸 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌹𑌾 𑌗𑍁𑌰𑍁𑌘𑍍𑌨𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌪𑌿𑌤𑍄𑌣𑌾𑌂 𑌘𑌾𑌤𑌕𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌥𑌾॥௨௪॥  
𑌶𑍍𑌲𑍋𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌧𑌂 𑌶𑍍𑌲𑍋𑌕𑌪𑌾𑌦𑌂 𑌵𑌾 𑌨𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌭𑌾𑌗𑌵𑌤𑍋𑌦𑍍𑌭𑌵𑌮𑍍।  
𑌵𑍈𑌶𑌾𑌖𑍇 𑌚 𑌪𑌠𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌰𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑍋 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌂 𑌚𑍋𑌪𑌪𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌤𑍇॥௨௫॥  
𑌯𑍋 𑌵𑍈 𑌭𑌾𑌗𑌵𑌤𑌂 𑌶𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌂 𑌶𑍃𑌣𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌯𑍇𑌤𑌦𑍍𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍇।  
𑌨 𑌪𑌾𑌪𑍈𑌰𑍍𑌲𑌿𑌪𑍍𑌯𑌤𑍇 𑌕𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌪𑌿 𑌪𑌦𑍍𑌮𑌪𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌮𑌿𑌵𑌾𑌮𑍍𑌭𑌸𑌾॥௨௬॥  
𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌂 𑌮𑌨𑍁𑌜𑍈𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌂 𑌕𑍈𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌸𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌮𑍇𑌵 𑌚।  
𑌕𑍈𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌤𑍋 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌭𑌾𑌵𑍋 𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑌨𑌿𑌷𑍇𑌵𑌣𑌾𑌤𑍍॥௨௭॥  
𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌜𑍍𑌞𑌾𑌨𑍇𑌨 𑌵𑍈 𑌮𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌯𑌾𑌗𑌮𑌰𑌣𑍇𑌨 𑌵𑌾।  
𑌅𑌥𑌵𑌾 𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌿 𑌵𑍈𑌶𑌾𑌖𑍇 𑌨𑌿𑌯𑌮𑍇𑌨 𑌜𑌲𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌲𑍁𑌤𑍇𑌃॥௨௮॥  
𑌨𑍀𑌲𑌵𑍃𑌷𑌂 𑌸𑌮𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌸𑍃𑌜𑍍𑌯 𑌵𑍈𑌶𑌾𑌖𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌚 𑌜𑌲𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌲𑍁𑌤𑍇𑌃।  
𑌸𑌮𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌬𑌨𑍍𑌧𑌨𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌮𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌃 𑌪𑍁𑌮𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌤𑌿 𑌪𑌰𑌂 𑌪𑌦𑌮𑍍॥௨௯॥  
𑌗𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑌵𑌤𑍍𑌸𑌾𑌂 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌜𑍇𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌯 𑌸𑍀𑌦𑌤𑍇 𑌚 𑌕𑍁𑌟𑍁𑌮𑍍𑌬𑌿𑌨𑍇।  
𑌇𑌹𑌾𑌪𑌮𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌨𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌮𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌃 𑌪𑌰𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌚 𑌪𑌰𑌂 𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌜𑍇𑌤𑍍॥௩௦॥  
𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌦𑌾𑌨𑌵𑌿𑌹𑍀𑌨𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌵𑍈𑌶𑌾𑌖𑍀 𑌚𑍈𑌵 𑌯𑍋 𑌨𑌯𑍇𑌤𑍍।  
𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌨𑌯𑍋𑌨𑌿𑌶𑌤𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌯 𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌠𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌜𑌾𑌯𑌤𑍇 𑌕𑍃𑌮𑌿𑌃॥௩௧॥  
𑌤𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌃 𑌕𑍋𑌟𑍍𑌯𑍋𑌽𑌰𑍍𑌧𑌕𑍋𑌟𑌿𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌤𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌭𑍁𑌵𑌨𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍇।  
𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌭𑍂𑌯 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑌾𑌞𑍍𑌚𑌕𑍍𑌰𑍁𑌃 𑌪𑌾𑌪𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌘𑌾𑌤𑌶𑌙𑍍𑌕𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌃॥௩௨॥  
𑌜𑌨𑌾 𑌅𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌸𑍁 𑌪𑌾𑌪𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌠𑌾 𑌵𑌿𑌸𑍃𑌜𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌕𑌂 𑌮𑌲𑌮𑍍।  
𑌤𑌦𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌕𑌂 𑌕𑌥𑌂 𑌗𑌚𑍍𑌛𑍇𑌦𑌿𑌤𑌿 𑌚𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌸𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌃॥௩௩॥  
𑌤𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌪𑌾𑌦𑌂 𑌹𑌰𑌿𑌂 𑌜𑌗𑍍𑌮𑍁𑌃 𑌶𑌰𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌶𑌰𑌣𑌂 𑌵𑌿𑌭𑍁𑌮𑍍।  
𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌚 𑌬𑌹𑍁𑌭𑌿𑌃 𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍈𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌯𑌾𑌮𑌾𑌸𑍁𑌰𑌞𑍍𑌜𑌸𑌾॥௩௪॥  
𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌦𑍇𑌵 𑌜𑌗𑌨𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌥 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌘𑍌𑌘𑌵𑌿𑌨𑌾𑌶𑌨।  
𑌜𑌨𑌾 𑌅𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌸𑍁 𑌪𑌾𑌪𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌠𑌾𑌃 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌪𑌾𑌪𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌶𑌃॥௩௫॥  
𑌵𑌿𑌸𑍃𑌜𑍍𑌯 𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌤𑍍𑌪𑌦𑌂 𑌯𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌦𑌾𑌜𑍍𑌞𑌾𑌧𑌾𑌰𑌿𑌣𑍋 𑌭𑍁𑌵𑌿।  
𑌅𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌕𑌂 𑌚𑍈𑌵 𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌪𑌾𑌪𑌂 𑌕𑌥𑌂 𑌗𑌚𑍍𑌛𑍇𑌜𑍍𑌜𑌨𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌦𑌨॥௩௬॥  
𑌤𑌦𑍁𑌪𑌾𑌯𑌂 𑌵𑌦𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌕𑌂 𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌤𑍍𑌪𑌾𑌦𑌶𑌰𑌣𑍈𑌷𑌿𑌣𑌾𑌮𑍍।  
𑌇𑌤𑌿 𑌤𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌥𑍈𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌿𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌭𑌗𑌵𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌭𑍂𑌤𑌭𑌾𑌵𑌨𑌃॥௩௭॥  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌹𑌸𑌨𑍍𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹 𑌤𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌮𑍇𑌘𑌗𑌮𑍍𑌭𑍀𑌰𑌯𑌾 𑌗𑌿𑌰𑌾।  
𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌭𑌗𑌵𑌾𑌨𑍁𑌵𑌾𑌚---  
𑌸𑌿𑌤𑍇 𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇 𑌮𑍇𑌷𑌸𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌯𑍇 𑌵𑍈𑌶𑌾𑌖𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍇𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍇॥௩௮॥  
𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌤𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌮𑌯𑍇 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑍇 𑌮𑌮𑌾𑌪𑌿 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌣𑌵𑌲𑍍𑌲𑌭𑍇।  
𑌯𑍂𑌯𑌂 𑌭𑌗𑍋𑌦𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌂 𑌬𑌹𑌿𑌃𑌸𑌂𑌸𑍍𑌥𑌜𑌲𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌲𑍁𑌤𑌾𑌃॥௩௯॥  
𑌵𑌿𑌮𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌘𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌰𑍂𑌪𑌾 𑌭𑌵𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌶𑍁 𑌸𑍁𑌨𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌲𑌾𑌃।  
𑌭𑌵𑌦𑍍𑌭𑌿𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌵𑌿𑌮𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌘𑍈𑌰𑍍𑌯𑍇 𑌨 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌤𑌾 𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍇॥௪௦॥  
𑌤𑍇𑌷𑍁 𑌤𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌠𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌪𑌾𑌪𑌂 𑌜𑌨𑍈𑌰𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌮𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌰𑍇𑌚𑌿𑌤𑌮𑍍।  
𑌇𑌤𑌿 𑌤𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌪𑌦𑍋 𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌂 𑌚 𑌵𑌰𑌂 𑌦𑌦𑍌॥௪௧॥  
𑌅𑌨𑍁𑌜𑍍𑌞𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌯 𑌚 𑌤𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌯𑍋𑌗𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍈𑌵𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌰𑌧𑍀𑌯𑌤।  
𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌧𑌾𑌮𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌪𑍁𑌨𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌯 𑌤𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌤𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌨𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌶𑌃॥௪௨॥  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌿𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌷𑌂 𑌤𑍁 𑌵𑍈𑌶𑌾𑌖𑍇 𑌤𑌥𑍈𑌵𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍇।  
𑌤𑍇𑌨𑌾𑌘𑍌𑌘𑌂 𑌵𑌿𑌮𑍁𑌚𑍍𑌯𑍈𑌵 𑌯𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌨𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌲𑌤𑌾𑌮𑌹𑍋॥௪௩॥  
𑌯𑍇 𑌤𑍁 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌨 𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌵𑍈𑌶𑌾𑌖𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍇।  
𑌤𑍇 𑌭𑌵𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌸𑌮𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌂 𑌜𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌂 𑌪𑌾𑌤𑌕𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌯𑌾𑌃॥௪௪॥  
𑌇𑌤𑌿 𑌶𑌾𑌪𑌂 𑌚 𑌤𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌹𑍍𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌤𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌂 𑌵𑌦𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌚।  
𑌨 𑌤𑍇𑌨 𑌸𑌦𑍃𑌶𑌃 𑌪𑌾𑌪𑍋 𑌯𑍋 𑌨 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍋 𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍇॥௪௫॥  
𑌵𑌿𑌚𑌾𑌰𑌿𑌤𑍇𑌷𑍁 𑌶𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌷𑍁 𑌨 𑌦𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌟𑍋 𑌨 𑌚 𑌵𑍈 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍁𑌤𑌃।  
𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍇 𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌦𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌚𑌨𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌕𑌮𑍍॥௪௬॥  
𑌅𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌥𑌾 𑌨𑌰𑌕𑌂 𑌯𑌾𑌤𑌿 𑌯𑌾𑌵𑌦𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌦𑌶।  
𑌇𑌤𑍍𑌯𑍇𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌮𑌾𑌖𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌤𑌂 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍁𑌤𑌕𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌮𑌤𑍇॥௪௭॥  
---𑌸𑍍𑌕𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌦-𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇 𑌵𑍈𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌵𑌖𑌣𑍍𑌡𑍇 𑌵𑍈𑌶𑌾𑌖𑌮𑌾𑌹𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌮𑍍𑌯𑍇 𑌪𑌞𑍍𑌚𑌵𑌿𑌂𑌶𑍋𑌽𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌃

e74aceeb8b.d: Budhaḥ sets into combustion (astamayaH), heading prāk (east), on 2025-Nov-15 16:56. At this moment budhaḥ is at anūrādhā-3 vr̥śchikaḥ (latitude 1°05′05.61″ S, moving vakra (retrograde)), magnitude +2.19, elongation 10°57′43.36″ E of the Sun. Combustion (mAudhyam) is generally considered to weaken a graha's ability to give full results in its significations; undertakings connected with budhaḥ are traditionally best avoided until it re-emerges.

e78114a218.d: Guruḥ rises out of combustion (udayaH), heading prāk (east), on 2027-Sep-14 08:49. At this moment guruḥ is at pūrvaphalgunī-1 siṁhaḥ (latitude 0°56′03.51″ N, moving r̥ju (direct)), magnitude -1.70, elongation 10°27′44.74″ W of the Sun. Emergence from combustion restores a graha's full strength; this is generally considered an auspicious time to begin activities connected with guruḥ's significations.

e79e3a88fd.b: Observed on Śukla-Ēkādaśī tithi of Pauṣaḥ (lunar) month (Aparāhṇaḥ/vyaapti).
e79e3a88fd.s:
𑌸𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌰𑍇---  
𑌅𑌮𑌾 𑌪𑌾𑌤𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌵𑍈𑌧𑍃𑌤𑌿𑌰𑍇𑌵 𑌚।  
𑌅𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌚𑍈𑌵 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌗𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌲𑌯𑌃॥  
𑌚𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌸𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌯𑍋𑌪𑌰𑌾𑌗𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌗𑌜𑌚𑍍𑌛𑌾𑌯𑌾 𑌤𑌥𑍈𑌵 𑌚।  
𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌣𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌪𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌃 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌕𑌾𑌲𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌕𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌃॥  
𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌰𑌾𑌦𑌯𑍋 𑌮𑌤𑍍𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇 𑌦𑌰𑍍𑌶𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌃---  
𑌆𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌯𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌛𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲𑌨𑌵𑌮𑍀 𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌕𑍀 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍀 𑌸𑌿𑌤𑌾।  
𑌤𑍃𑌤𑍀𑌯𑌾 𑌚𑍈𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌸𑌿𑌤𑌾 𑌭𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌪𑌦𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌚॥  
𑌫𑌾𑌲𑍍𑌗𑍁𑌨𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌯𑌮𑌾𑌵𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌪𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌯𑍈𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍀 𑌸𑌿𑌤𑌾।  
𑌆𑌷𑌾𑌢𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌪𑌿 𑌦𑌶𑌮𑍀 𑌮𑌾𑌘𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌮𑍀॥  
𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌵𑌣𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌮𑍀 𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌾 𑌤𑌥𑌾𑌽𑌽𑌷𑌾𑌢𑍀 𑌚 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌿𑌮𑌾।  
𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌕𑍀 𑌫𑌾𑌲𑍍𑌗𑍁𑌨𑍀 𑌚𑍈𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍀 𑌜𑍍𑌯𑍈𑌷𑍍𑌠𑍀 𑌪𑌞𑍍𑌚𑌦𑌶𑍀 𑌸𑌿𑌤𑌾॥  
𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌰𑌾𑌦𑌯𑌶𑍍𑌚𑍈𑌤𑍇 𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌯𑌕𑌾𑌰𑌕𑌾𑌃।  
𑌕𑍃𑌤𑌂 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌂 𑌵𑌿𑌧𑌾𑌨𑍇𑌨 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌷𑍁 𑌯𑍁𑌗𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌷𑍁॥  
𑌹𑌾𑌯𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌸𑌾𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌂 𑌪𑌿𑌤𑍄𑌣𑌾𑌂 𑌤𑍃𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌦𑌂 𑌭𑌵𑍇𑌤𑍍।  
𑌆𑌸𑍁 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌜𑌪𑍋 𑌹𑍋𑌮𑌃 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌨𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯 𑌕𑌲𑍍𑌪𑌤𑍇॥  
𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌭𑌾𑌰𑌤𑍇𑌽𑌪𑌿---   
𑌯𑌾 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌯𑍁𑌗𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌤𑌿𑌥𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌸𑍁 𑌮𑌾𑌨𑌵𑌃।  
𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌭𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌚 𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌚 𑌤𑌦𑌨𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌲𑌭𑍇𑌤𑍍॥  
𑌕𑌾𑌲𑌾𑌦𑌰𑍍𑌶𑍇𑌽𑌪𑌿---  
𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌸𑍁 𑌯𑍁𑌗𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌸𑍁 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌃 𑌸𑌲𑌿𑌲𑌾𑌞𑍍𑌜𑌲𑌿𑌃।  
𑌸𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌵𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌷𑌿𑌕𑍀 𑌤𑍃𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌂 𑌪𑌿𑌤𑍄𑌣𑌾𑌮𑌾𑌵𑌹𑍇𑌤𑍍 𑌪𑌰𑌾𑌮𑍍॥  
𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌸𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌬𑍍𑌦𑌿𑌕𑍀 𑌤𑍃𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌂 𑌕𑍃𑌤𑌂 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌂 𑌯𑌥𑌾𑌵𑌿𑌧𑌿।  
𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌦𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌜𑌪𑍋 𑌹𑍋𑌮𑌃 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌨𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯 𑌕𑌲𑍍𑌪𑌤𑍇॥  
𑌪𑍁𑌰𑍁𑌷𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌚𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌮𑌣𑍌 𑌮𑌨𑍁𑌃---  
𑌸𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌗𑍁𑌣𑌿𑌤𑌂 𑌦𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌭𑌵𑍇𑌦𑍍𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌂 𑌯𑍁𑌗𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌷𑍁।  
𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌮 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌕𑌂 𑌚𑍈𑌵 𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌰𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌷𑍁॥

e7a3325afc.d: Śaniḥ rises out of combustion (udayaH), heading prāk (east), on 2026-Apr-18 03:44. At this moment śaniḥ is at uttaraprōṣṭhapadā-4 mīnaḥ (latitude 2°08′51.09″ S, moving r̥ju (direct)), magnitude +0.93, elongation 20°23′34.17″ W of the Sun. Emergence from combustion restores a graha's full strength; this is generally considered an auspicious time to begin activities connected with śaniḥ's significations.

e7a56ea10d.d: When a tripādanakṣatra is conjoined with a bhadrā tithi i.e. dvitīyā, saptamī or dvādaśī, and this falls on a Tuesday, Sunday or Saturday, it is known as a tripuṣkara-yōgaḥ. When only two of these coincide, it is known as dvipuṣkara. These are specially auspicious times, and are excluded for aparakarmas such as ūnamāsikaśrāddham.
e7a56ea10d.s:
𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌪𑌾𑌦𑌰𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌂 𑌤𑌿𑌥𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌭𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌾 𑌭𑍌𑌮𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌕𑌶𑌨𑌿𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌰𑍇।  
𑌤𑌦𑌾 𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌪𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌕𑌰𑍋 𑌯𑍋𑌗𑍋 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌯𑍋𑌰𑍍𑌯𑍋𑌗𑍇 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌪𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌕𑌰𑌃॥  
---𑌜𑍍𑌯𑍋𑌤𑌿𑌷𑍇  
𑌯𑌦𑌾 𑌭𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌿𑌥𑍀𑌨𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍 𑌪𑌾𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌰𑍇𑌣 𑌸𑌂𑌯𑍁𑌤𑌿𑌃।  
𑌖𑌣𑍍𑌡𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌿𑌤𑍀𑌶𑌯𑍋𑌗𑌶𑍍𑌚𑍇𑌤𑍍 𑌸 𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌯𑍋𑌗𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌪𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌕𑌰𑌃॥  
𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌤𑍀𑌯𑌾𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌮𑍀𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍀𑌨𑌾𑌂 𑌭𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌿𑌥𑍀𑌨𑌾𑌂 𑌕𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌕𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌨𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌸𑍂𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌰𑌫𑌲𑍍𑌗𑍁𑌨𑍀𑌵𑌿𑌶𑌾𑌖𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌰𑌾𑌷𑌾𑌢𑌾 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌭𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌪𑌦𑌾 𑌨𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌣𑌾𑌂 𑌭𑌾𑌨𑍁𑌭𑍌𑌮𑌶𑌨𑍈𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌰𑌵𑌾𑌰𑌾𑌣𑌾𑌂 𑌚 𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑌾𑌣𑌾𑌂 𑌮𑍇𑌲𑌨𑍇 𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌪𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌕𑌰𑌮𑍍।  
𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌯𑍋𑌰𑍍𑌮𑍇𑌲𑌨𑍇 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌪𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌕𑌰𑌮𑍍।   
𑌭𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌾 𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌪𑌦𑌨𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌂 𑌭𑌾𑌨𑍁𑌭𑍌𑌮𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌕𑌿𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌰𑌾𑌃।  
𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌪𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌕𑌰𑌾 𑌇𑌤𑌿 𑌖𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌤𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌤𑍂𑌨𑌂 𑌨 𑌕𑌾𑌰𑌯𑍇𑌤𑍍॥  
---𑌇𑌤𑌿 𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌰𑌣𑌾𑌤𑍍  
(𑌸𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑌿𑌮𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌫𑌲𑍇 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌕𑌾𑌣𑍍𑌡𑍇 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌭𑌾𑌗𑍇 𑌪𑍃 ௪௯௧ (SVR))

e7a6bab24e.b: Observed on Maghā nakshatra of Makaraḥ (sidereal solar) month (Prātaḥ/paraviddha).

e7b15e3e4c.b: Observed on Śukla-Prathamā tithi of Āṣāḍhaḥ (lunar) month (Aparāhṇaḥ/vyaapti). The event occurred in 3649 (Kali era).
e7b15e3e4c.d: The noble son of Śrīkṛṣṇa of Śrīmuṣṇa by name Śivasāmbha who went round the earth thrice, became a disciple of Śrīcitrukha through initiation, and later became the head of Śrī Śārada maṭha. He (Śrī Citsukhendra), whose biography was composed by Mantha in his work titled Siddhajaya adorned the Pīṭha for twenty-one years and attained immortal state. He, the austere, Saccidānandaghana attained immortality in the form of Śivaliṅga on the first day of the bright fortnight in the month of Āṣāḍha of Prabhava year in the Śaka era 470.
e7b15e3e4c.s:
𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌮𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌤𑌨𑌯𑌃 𑌶𑌿𑌵𑌸𑌾𑌮𑍍𑌬𑌨𑌾𑌮𑌾 𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌦𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌿𑌣𑌿𑌤𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌮𑌹𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌮𑌾।  
𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌚𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌸𑍁𑌖𑍇𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌯𑌮𑌿𑌨𑌃 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌤𑌶𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌭𑌾𑌵𑌃 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌶𑌾𑌰𑌦𑌾𑌮𑌠𑌵𑌿𑌭𑍁𑌃 𑌸𑌮𑌭𑍂𑌤𑍍 𑌸 𑌶𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌃॥௫௨॥  
𑌯𑌦𑍀𑌯𑌵𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌂 𑌨𑌿𑌬𑌬𑌨𑍍𑌧 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌥𑍋 𑌨𑌿𑌬𑌨𑍍𑌧𑌨𑍇 𑌸𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌜𑌯𑌾𑌭𑌿𑌧𑌾𑌨𑍇।  
𑌸 𑌵𑌿𑌂𑌶𑌤𑌿𑌂 𑌸𑍈𑌕𑌸𑌮𑌾𑌃 𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌪𑍀𑌠𑍇 𑌨𑌿𑌷𑌦𑍍𑌯 𑌨𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌮𑍍 𑌅𑌵𑌾𑌪 𑌸𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌃॥௫௩॥  
𑌅𑌧𑌿𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌤𑌿𑌕𑍇 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌶𑍍𑌶𑌿𑌰𑌸𑍍𑌕𑍇 (௪௭௦) 𑌸𑌚𑍍𑌚𑌿𑌦𑌾𑌨𑌨𑍍𑌦𑌘𑌨𑌃 𑌸 𑌸𑌨𑍍 𑌶𑌕𑌾𑌬𑍍𑌦𑍇।  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌭𑌵𑍇 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌭𑌵𑌨𑍍 𑌶𑍁𑌚𑌿𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌶𑍁𑌚𑍍𑌯𑍋𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌥𑌮𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌪𑍃𑌥𑍁𑌲𑌿𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌤𑌾𑌮𑍍 𑌅𑌵𑌾𑌪𑌤𑍍॥௫௪॥  
—𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌶𑍍𑌲𑍋𑌕𑌮𑌞𑍍𑌜𑌰𑍀

e7c9205619.b: Observed on Śravaṇaḥ nakshatra of Siṁhaḥ (sidereal solar) month (Prātaḥ/paraviddha).

e7f24d7a78.d: Guruḥ enters vArdhakya (old age) on 2027-Aug-03 10:02, 15 days before it sets into combustion (mAudhyam). At this moment guruḥ is at maghā-3 siṁhaḥ (latitude 0°54′24.95″ N, moving r̥ju (direct)), magnitude -1.72, elongation 21°01′09.67″ E of the Sun. A graha in vArdhakya is considered weakened, giving reduced results, though less so than in outright mAudhya.

e8190cb266.d: Śukraḥ's vArdhakya ends on 2025-Dec-03 06:43, as it sets into combustion (mAudhyam). At this moment śukraḥ is at anūrādhā-2 vr̥śchikaḥ (latitude 0°37′43.66″ N, moving r̥ju (direct)), magnitude -3.92, elongation 8°21′58.55″ W of the Sun.

e81a8eb63d.d: Śukraḥ sets into combustion (astamayaH), heading prāk (east), on 2026-Oct-18 23:16. At this moment śukraḥ is at svātī-1 tulā (latitude 7°14′17.07″ S, moving vakra (retrograde)), magnitude -4.12, elongation 11°12′18.23″ E of the Sun. Combustion (mAudhyam) is generally considered to weaken a graha's ability to give full results in its significations; undertakings connected with śukraḥ are traditionally best avoided until it re-emerges.

e830197eef.d: Budhaḥ rises out of combustion (udayaH), heading prāk (east), on 2025-Jun-11 11:19. At this moment budhaḥ is at ārdrā-2 mithunam (latitude 1°56′49.42″ N, moving r̥ju (direct)), magnitude -1.00, elongation 14°06′13.36″ E of the Sun. Emergence from combustion restores a graha's full strength; this is generally considered an auspicious time to begin activities connected with budhaḥ's significations.

e8719d4dab.b: Observed on Śukla-Aṣṭamī tithi of Āṣāḍhaḥ (lunar) month (Sūryōdayaḥ/puurvaviddha).
e8719d4dab.s:
𑌨𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌯𑌾𑌮𑍃𑌤𑍇 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑍀𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇---  
𑌅𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌚 𑌤𑌥𑌾𑌽𑌽𑌷𑌾𑌢𑍇 𑌨𑌿𑌶𑌾𑌤𑍋𑌯𑍇𑌨 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌪𑌯𑍇𑌤𑍍।  
𑌮𑌹𑌿𑌷𑌘𑍍𑌨𑍀𑌮𑌿𑌤𑌿 𑌶𑍇𑌷𑌃। 𑌨𑌿𑌶𑌾 𑌹𑌰𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌾।  
𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌯𑌂 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌚 𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍈𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌨𑍍𑌦𑌨𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌂 𑌵𑌿𑌲𑍇𑌪𑌯𑍇𑌤𑍍।  
𑌧𑍂𑌪𑌚𑌨𑍍𑌦𑌨𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍈𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌲𑌕𑍈𑌃 𑌸𑌿𑌤𑌸𑌿𑌹𑍍𑌲𑌕𑍈𑌃॥

e88eb9eb6d.d: Born on the banks of river Tapati as the son of Śaṅkarakeśavasya and avowed to rigid celibacy Śrī Acyutakeśava, known as Ujjvalaśaṅkara, after being initiated by Gīṣpati, patronised by Vañcīśavara, uprooted the rival schools and with fame the great saint reached Kashmir. Then having spent thirty-eight years in the Pīṭha of the Universal Preceptor, He merged in Brahman, the eternal free from joy and sorrow and the everlasting on the eighth day of the bright fortnight in Vṛṣa month of the year Akṣaya in the Kali era 3468 in the place called Kalāpur in Kashmir.

e896e1d609.d:
Lieutenant Manoj Kumar Pandey, a young officer of the 1/11 Gorkha Rifles, died conquering  Jubar Top from pAkistAni jihAdists on this day.

On the night of 2/3 July 1999, 'B' Company of 1/11 Gorkha Rifles approached Jubar top along a narrow ridge. He surged ahead of his troops and charged at the enemy with a full-throated battle cry (जय महाकाली! आयो गारखाली!) through a hail of bullets. Fearlessly assaulting the first enemy position, he killed two enemy personnel and destroyed the second position by killing two more. Although wounded in the shoulder and leg, he pressed on his solitary charge with grim determination, until he closed in on the first bunker. He continued to lead the assault on the fourth position urging his men and destroyed the same with a grenade, even as he got a fatal Medium Machine Gun burst on his forehead.

Entries in Pandey's personal diary:

- 'If death strikes before I prove my blood, I promise (swear), I will kill death!'
- 'Some goals are so worthy, it's glorious even to fail!'

e8ee3c0583.b: Observed on Paurṇamāsī tithi of Bhādrapadaḥ (lunar) month (Sūryōdayaḥ/paraviddha).
e8ee3c0583.s:
𑌪𑌰𑌵𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌾 𑌗𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌯𑌾। 𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌚𑍋𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌂 𑌭𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌯𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌰𑍇।  
𑌸𑍍𑌕𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍇---  
𑌭𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌪𑌦𑌶𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌿𑌮𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌮𑍁𑌮𑌾𑌮𑌹𑍇𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌰𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌂 𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌮𑍍।  
𑌸𑌾 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌣𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌪𑌿𑌨𑍀   
𑌨𑌭𑌸𑍍𑌯𑍇 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌿𑌮𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌤𑍁 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌨𑍇 𑌚 𑌵𑌿𑌶𑍇𑌷𑌤𑌃।  
𑌉𑌮𑌾𑌮𑌹𑍇𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌰𑌂 𑌨𑌾𑌮 𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌂 𑌯𑌜𑍍𑌞𑌫𑌲𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌦𑌮𑍍॥ 𑌇𑌤𑌿।  
𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌿 𑌭𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌪𑌦𑍇 𑌶𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲𑍇 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌮𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑌿𑌨𑍋𑌦𑌯𑍇।  
𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍈𑌵 𑌵𑌿𑌧𑌿𑌵𑌦𑍁𑌮𑌾𑌮𑌾𑌹𑍇𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌰𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌮𑍍॥ 𑌇𑌤𑌿।  
𑌇𑌨𑍋𑌦𑌯 𑌇𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌿𑌮𑌾 𑌯𑌾 𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌯𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌤𑍌 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌦𑌶𑍀𑌸𑌹𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌂 𑌵𑌿𑌹𑌾𑌯 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌿𑌪𑌤𑍍𑌸𑌹𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌮𑍇𑌵  
𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌿𑌮𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌮𑍁𑌮𑌾𑌮𑌹𑍇𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌰𑌾𑌖𑍍𑌯𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌂 𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍। 𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌮𑍁𑌹𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌵𑍇𑌧𑍋𑌽𑌪𑍇𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌣𑍀𑌯𑌃। 𑌇𑌨𑍋𑌦𑌯  
𑌇𑌤𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌯𑍇𑌽𑌪𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌦𑌯𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌤𑍌 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌤𑍍 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍈𑌵𑍇𑌤𑌿 𑌯𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌮𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌪𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑌃।

e957f7437b.d: On this day died the selfless patriot Vasudev Balwant Phadke, who single handedly tried to resist the might of British Empire. Phadke was transported to jail at Aden, but escaped from the prison by taking the door off from its hinges on 13 February 1883. He was soon recaptured and then went on a hunger strike, dying on 17 February 1883.

e9887dffd3.s:
𑌫𑌾𑌲𑍍𑌗𑍁𑌨𑌶𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌕𑌾𑌮𑌦𑌹𑌨𑌂 𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌮𑍍। 𑌸𑌾 𑌮𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌰𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌪𑌿𑌨𑍀 𑌗𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌯𑌾। 𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌚𑍋𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌂 𑌸𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌰𑍇---  
𑌫𑌲𑍍𑌗𑍁𑌨𑍇 𑌶𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇 𑌤𑍁 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌨𑌿𑌶𑌿।  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌿𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌷𑌂 𑌦𑌹𑍇𑌤𑍍 𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌕𑍍 𑌮𑍃𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌯𑌂 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌥𑌂 𑌨𑍃𑌪॥ 𑌇𑌤𑌿।  
𑌅𑌰𑍍𑌧𑌰𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌧𑌾---𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍇𑌦𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌃 𑌪𑌰𑍇𑌦𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌰𑍁𑌭𑌯𑍇𑌦𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌰𑌨𑍁𑌭𑌯𑍇𑌦𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌶𑍍𑌚।  
𑌉𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌂 𑌚 𑌭𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇---  
𑌯𑌦𑌾 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌦𑌶𑍀 𑌰𑌾𑌜𑌨𑍍 𑌤𑌪𑌸𑍍𑌯𑍇 𑌶𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌕𑍇।  
𑌅𑌰𑍍𑌧𑌰𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌯𑍁𑌤𑌾 𑌯𑌾 𑌵𑍈 𑌦𑌾𑌹𑌯𑍋𑌗𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌹𑌿 𑌸𑌾 𑌤𑌿𑌥𑌿𑌃॥ 𑌇𑌤𑌿।  
𑌤𑍃𑌤𑍀𑌯𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌯𑍋𑌰𑌪𑌿 𑌪𑌰𑌾 𑌗𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌯𑌾।   
𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌚 𑌸𑍍𑌕𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍇---  
𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌯𑍇 𑌨𑌿𑌶𑍀𑌥𑍇 𑌚𑍇𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌤𑍇 𑌚 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌦𑌶𑍀।  
𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌪𑌰𑍈𑌵 𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌦𑌹𑌨𑍇 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌥𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌚॥ 𑌇𑌤𑌿।  
𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌯𑍇 𑌯𑌦𑌾 𑌨 𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌨𑌿𑌶𑍀𑌥𑍇 𑌚 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌦𑌶𑍀।  
𑌤𑌦𑌾 𑌗𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌪𑌰𑍈𑌵 𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍 𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍈𑌵 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌦𑌹𑍇𑌤𑍍 𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌰𑌮𑍍॥ 𑌇𑌤𑌿।  
𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌦𑌿𑌨𑍇 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌥𑌦𑌹𑌨𑍇 𑌦𑍋𑌷𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌰𑌣𑌾𑌤𑍍।  
𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌚 𑌸𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌰𑍇---  
𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌦𑌶𑍀𑌂 𑌪𑌰𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌜𑍍𑌯 𑌹𑍍𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌥𑌾 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌦𑌹𑍇𑌤𑍍 𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌰𑌮𑍍।  
𑌗𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌮𑌾𑌧𑌿𑌪𑌤𑌿𑌨𑌾𑌶𑌃 𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍 𑌗𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌗𑍍𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌵𑌚𑌨𑌂 𑌯𑌥𑌾॥ 𑌇𑌤𑌿।  
𑌕𑍍𑌵𑌚𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌦𑍇𑌶𑍇 𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍋𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌷𑍁 𑌆𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌷𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌪𑌰𑍍𑌕𑌰𑌹𑌿𑌤𑌦𑌿𑌨𑍇 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌥𑌂 𑌦𑌗𑍍𑌧𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌵𑍇𑌧𑌰𑌹𑌿𑌤𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌰𑌫𑌲𑍍𑌗𑍁𑌨𑍀𑌯𑍁𑌤𑌦𑌿𑌨𑍇 𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌡𑍋𑌲𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌸𑌵𑌂 𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿। 𑌕𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑌮𑌤𑌮𑌵𑌲𑌮𑍍𑌬𑍍𑌯 𑌰𑌾𑌮𑌾𑌨𑍁𑌜𑌸𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌨𑌾𑌮𑌿𑌦𑌂 𑌮𑌤𑌮𑍍।

e9943c6abf.b: Observed on Svātī nakshatra of Mīnaḥ (sidereal solar) month (Prātaḥ/paraviddha).
e9943c6abf.d:
Between the 6th and 9th centuries, in South India, there existed 63 ardent devotees of Bhagavan Shiva, collectively known as the Nayanmars. These devout individuals, hailing from various walks of life including potters, fishermen, farmers, merchants, priests, hunters, and washermen, created devotional songs still sung by followers around the globe. Among these Nayanmars, Appar, Sambandar, and Sundarar, known for their Thevaram hymns, along with Manikkavasagar, are distinguished as the Samayacharyas or the ‘The Four’ (nālvar) revered teachers of the faith. They were instrumental in promoting the Shaiva Siddhanta philosophy and culture, effectively challenging the spread of Jainism and Buddhism. Their teachings centered around the concept that Shiva embodies love, and that embracing love for all beings and existence is essential in connecting with Shiva, the Supreme Being.

Karaikal Ammaiyar, originally named Punithavathy, was born into a prosperous Vaisya family. Her parents, Danadathan and his wife, were devout and virtuous. Punithavathy, a fervent devotee of Bhagavan Shiva from childhood, married Paramadattan, a wealthy merchant. They led an exemplary life until an incident tested her devotion.

One day, after receiving two mangoes from Paramadattan, Punithavathy encountered a famished Shiva Yogi and offered him one of the mangoes. When Paramadattan requested the second mango at mealtime, Punithavathy prayed for divine assistance. Miraculously, another mango appeared, which she served to her husband. Astounded by its divine taste, Paramadattan questioned its origin. Upon learning the truth, he found it inconceivable to live as her husband, considering her divine qualities.

Paramadattan left for a foreign land under the guise of business, settled in the Pandyan kingdom, remarried, and named his daughter after Punithavathy, out of his deep regard for her. When Punithavathy's relatives learned of his whereabouts, they took her to meet him. Paramadattan, receiving her with his new family, fell at her feet, worshipping her as a goddess.

Realising Paramadattan's perception of her, Punithavathy prayed to Bhagavan Shiva for a demoniacal form to renounce her physical charm. Her prayer was answered, transforming her into a skeletal form. She then journeyed to Kailasa, the abode of Bhagavan Shiva and Parvati. Overflowing with devotion, and considering the sacredness of Kailasa, she considered it a sin to set her foot on the holy mountain, and travelled the final stretch on her head! As Parvati Devi was astounded by her strange form and unique devotion, Bhagavan Shiva narrated the greatness of Ammaiyar to Her.

Acknowledging her exceptional devotion, Bhagavan Shiva welcomed her warmly and offered her a boon. Punithavathy requested perpetual, undiluted devotion to Bhagavan Shiva, freedom from rebirth, and the privilege to sing his praises during his cosmic dance. Bhagavan Shiva granted her wishes and directed her to Thiruvalangadu, where she spent the rest of her life singing hymns in praise of Bhagavan.
e9943c6abf.r: - 63 Nayanmar Saints by Swami Sivananda, published by The Divine Life Society

e9a7e0b452.d: Budhaḥ sets into combustion (astamayaH), heading prāk (east), on 2026-Jul-06 09:05. At this moment budhaḥ is at punarvasuḥ-4 karkaṭaḥ (latitude 3°46′36.93″ S, moving vakra (retrograde)), magnitude +3.62, elongation 11°16′39.63″ E of the Sun. Combustion (mAudhyam) is generally considered to weaken a graha's ability to give full results in its significations; undertakings connected with budhaḥ are traditionally best avoided until it re-emerges.

e9de72b85b.s:
𑌉𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌞𑍍𑌚 𑌭𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌯𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌰𑍇---  
𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌵𑌣𑌶𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌿𑌮𑍋𑌪𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌭𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌗𑌵𑌦𑌿𑌨𑍇 𑌵𑌰𑌲𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌮𑍀𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌂 𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌮𑍍।  
𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌵𑌣𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌸𑌿𑌤𑍇 𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌿𑌮𑍋𑌪𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌭𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌗𑌵𑍇।  
𑌵𑌰𑌲𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌮𑍀𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌂 𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌮𑍋𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌪𑌤𑍍𑌫𑌲𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌦𑌮𑍍॥ 𑌇𑌤𑌿।  
𑌯𑌦𑌾 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌿𑌮𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌮𑍇𑌵 𑌭𑍃𑌗𑍁𑌵𑌾𑌰𑌃 𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌭𑌵𑌤𑌿 𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌨𑍇𑌵 𑌦𑌿𑌨𑍇 𑌵𑌰𑌲𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌮𑍀𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌂 𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌮𑍍।  
𑌨𑍋𑌪𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌭𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌗𑌵𑌦𑌿𑌨𑍇। 𑌉𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌂 𑌚 𑌕𑍌𑌮𑍁𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑍍---  
𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌿𑌨𑍍 𑌵𑍈 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌵𑌣𑍇 𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌿 𑌶𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌤𑍁 𑌭𑍃𑌗𑍋𑌰𑍍𑌦𑌿𑌨𑍇।  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌰𑌭𑍍𑌯 𑌤𑌦𑍍𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌂 𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌵𑌰𑌲𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌯𑌤𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌮𑌭𑌿𑌃॥ 𑌇𑌤𑌿।

ea122ef076.d: The three days around the Ashtaka Shraaddha of  mārgaśīrṣa, pauṣa and māgha month are anadhyayana days, where one is not supposed to learn the Vedas.
ea122ef076.s:
𑌮𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌗𑌶𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌷𑍇 𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌪𑍌𑌷𑍇 𑌮𑌾𑌘𑌮𑌾𑌸𑍇 𑌤𑌥𑍈𑌵 𑌚॥௭௬॥  
𑌤𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌰𑍋𑌽𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑌾𑌃 𑌸𑌮𑌾𑌖𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌤𑌾𑌃 𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇𑌷𑍁 𑌸𑍂𑌰𑌿𑌭𑌿𑌃।  
---𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌕𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇 𑌷𑌟𑍍‌𑌸𑌾𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑌂𑌹𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌮𑍁𑌪𑌰𑌿𑌵𑌿𑌭𑌾𑌗𑍇 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌦𑌶𑍋𑌽𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑍇

ea19476994.d: Observed on the first Friday following the transit of Sun into tulārāśī. Three Vratas are very special for Subrahmanya---this one, the regular kr̥ttikā vratam, and skandaṣaṣṭhivratam.
ea19476994.s:
𑌅𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌦𑍍𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌵𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑌿 𑌸𑍁𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌵𑍈 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌜𑌾𑌃।  
𑌤𑍁𑌲𑌾𑌰𑌾𑌶𑌿𑌂 𑌗𑌤𑍇 𑌸𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌯 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌿𑌨𑍍 𑌭𑍃𑌗𑍁𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌰𑍇॥௧॥  
𑌸𑌮𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌥𑌾𑌯 𑌶𑍁𑌚𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌭𑍂𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌤𑌰𑍇𑌵 𑌷𑌡𑌾𑌨𑌨𑌮𑍍।  
𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌹𑍃𑌦𑌬𑍍𑌜𑌨𑌿𑌲𑌯𑍇 𑌨𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌮 𑌸𑌮𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌯 𑌚॥௨॥  
𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌂 𑌚𑌰𑍇𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌧𑌾𑌨𑍇𑌨 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌪𑌾𑌪𑌹𑌰𑌂 𑌪𑌰𑌮𑍍।  
𑌕𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌕𑌾𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌚𑍍𑌚 𑌸𑍍𑌕𑌨𑍍𑌦𑌷𑌷𑍍𑌠𑌿𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌂 𑌪𑌰𑌮𑍍॥௩॥  
𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌣𑌿 𑌯𑍇 𑌮𑌰𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌰𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌗𑌮𑌮𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌗𑌤𑌃।  
𑌤𑍇 𑌭𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌵𑌿𑌪𑍁𑌲𑌾𑌨𑍍 𑌭𑍋𑌗𑌾𑌨𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌮𑍋𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌂 𑌗𑍁𑌹𑌾𑌜𑍍𑌞𑌯𑌾॥௪॥  
𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑌯𑍋 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌰𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌵𑍈𑌤𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌭𑍂𑌸𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌃।  
𑌜𑌘𑍍𑌨𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌦𑍈𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌘𑍋𑌰𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌰𑌣𑌮𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌗𑌤𑌾𑌨𑍍 𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾॥௫॥  
𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌤𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌂 𑌚 𑌦𑌿𑌶𑌾𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌦𑌿𑌕𑍍𑌪𑌾𑌲𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑍁𑌨𑌰𑌪𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌤।  
𑌮𑍁𑌚𑍁𑌕𑍁𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍋 𑌮𑌹𑍀𑌪𑌾𑌲𑌃 𑌶𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍂𑌞𑍍𑌜𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌰𑌣𑍇 𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾॥௬॥  
𑌗𑌾𑌣𑌾𑌧𑌿𑌪𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌪 𑌚𑌰𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌵𑍈𑌤𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌭𑍂𑌸𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌃।  
𑌨𑌾𑌰𑌦𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌮𑍁𑌖𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍇 𑌤𑌾𑌪𑌸𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌮𑌧𑍀𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌰𑌾𑌃॥௭॥  
𑌨𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌤𑍁𑌲𑌂 𑌪𑍁𑌨𑌰𑌾𑌵𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌦𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌲𑌭𑌮𑍍।  
𑌪𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌯𑍁𑌃 𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾 𑌕𑍇𑌚𑌿𑌦𑌪𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌣𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌮𑌾𑌃॥௮॥  
𑌐𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌜𑍍𑌞𑌾𑌨𑌯𑍋𑌗𑌾𑌂𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌮𑍋𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌂 𑌚𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌃 𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾 𑌪𑌰𑍇।  
𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌵𑍇𑌤𑍇𑌷𑍁 𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌂 𑌚𑍈𑌕𑌂 𑌯𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌰𑍇𑌦𑍍𑌗𑍁𑌹𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌮𑌤𑌮𑍍॥௯॥  
𑌸 𑌲𑌬𑍍𑌧𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌵𑌾𑌞𑍍𑌛𑌿𑌤𑌂 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌂 𑌶𑌿𑌵𑌲𑍋𑌕𑌮𑌨𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌮𑌮𑍍।  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌯 𑌮𑍋𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌂 𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌜𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌗𑍁𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌯𑍈𑌵 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌸𑌾𑌦𑌤𑌃॥௧௦॥  
𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌣𑌿 𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌯𑍋 𑌮𑌰𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌰𑌤𑌿 𑌸𑍍𑌕𑌨𑍍𑌦𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌮𑌤𑌮𑍍।  
𑌮𑌾𑌹𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌕𑍋 𑌵𑍇𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌗𑍁𑌹𑌤𑍁𑌲𑍍𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌭𑍂𑌸𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌃॥௧௧॥  
𑌯 𑌇𑌮𑌂 𑌪𑌠𑌤𑍇𑌽𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌂 𑌯𑌃 𑌶𑍃𑌣𑍋𑌤𑌿 𑌗𑍁𑌹𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌯𑌮𑍍।  
𑌸 𑌭𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌵𑌿𑌪𑍁𑌲𑌾𑌨𑍍 𑌭𑍋𑌗𑌾𑌨𑍍 𑌮𑍋𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌂 𑌯𑌾𑌤𑌿 𑌮𑌹𑍀𑌸𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌃॥   
𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀 𑌸𑍍𑌕𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍇 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇 𑌶𑌙𑍍𑌕𑌰𑌸𑌂𑌹𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌶𑌿𑌵𑌰𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌖𑌣𑍍𑌡𑍇 𑌉𑌪𑌦𑍇𑌶𑌕𑌾𑌣𑍍𑌡𑍇 𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌂𑌶𑍋𑌽𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑍇

ea3004339c.b: Observed on Śukla-Prathamā tithi of Āṣāḍhaḥ (lunar) month (Sūryōdayaḥ/puurvaviddha).
ea3004339c.d: Āṣāḍha-māsaḥ begins today --- In the Mahābhārata, it is said that one who observes a disciplined ekabhakta (one meal a day) fast throughout the month of Āṣāḍha, without lethargy (atandritaḥ), will be blessed with abundant grain, wealth, and many children. In the Vāmana Purāṇa, it is said that, to please Vāmana in the month of Āṣāḍha, one should offer — with devotion — a pair of sandals, an umbrella, salt, and āmalaka fruits.
ea3004339c.s:
𑌆𑌷𑌾𑌢𑌕𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌭𑌾𑌰𑌤𑍇---  
𑌆𑌷𑌾𑌢𑌮𑍇𑌕𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍇𑌨 𑌸𑍍𑌥𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌮𑌤𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌤𑌃।  
𑌬𑌹𑍁𑌧𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌯𑍋 𑌬𑌹𑍁𑌧𑌨𑍋 𑌬𑌹𑍁𑌪𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌜𑌾𑌯𑌤𑍇॥  
𑌵𑌾𑌮𑌨𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇---  
𑌉𑌪𑌾𑌨𑌦𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌗𑌲𑌂 𑌛𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌂 𑌲𑌵𑌣𑌾𑌮𑌲𑌕𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌚।  
𑌆𑌷𑌾𑌢𑍇 𑌵𑌾𑌮𑌨𑌪𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌤𑍍𑌯𑍈 𑌦𑌾𑌤𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌤𑍁 𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌤𑌃॥ 𑌇𑌤𑌿।

ea6c99743f.d: Upavāsam with only water and next day pāraṇa gives ārōgyam
ea6c99743f.s:
𑌆𑌷𑌾𑌢 𑌶𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲𑌷𑌷𑍍𑌠𑍀 𑌤𑍁 𑌤𑌿𑌥𑌿𑌃 𑌕𑍌𑌮𑌾𑌰𑌿𑌲𑌾 𑌸𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑌾।  
𑌕𑍁𑌮𑌾𑌰𑌮𑌰𑍍𑌚𑌯𑍇𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍋𑌪𑍇𑌷𑍍𑌯 𑌵𑍈 𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌮𑍍॥

ea828ed132.d:
Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy or majjari Narasimha Reddy, son of a pALEyagAra, was executed in Koilkuntla in front of a crowd of over 2000 people.

He and his commander-in-chief Vadde Obanna were at the heart of the rebellion against British in 1847, where 5,000 peasants rose up against the British East India Company in Kurnool district, Rayalaseema Region of Andhra Pradesh. They were protesting against the changes introduced by the British to the traditional agrarian system in the first half of the nineteenth century. British kept his head on the fort wall in public view until 1877.

eabdca83bb.d: Iṣṭiḥ is performed on this day by those following the bōdhāyana/kātyāyana sūtras. This difference happens because chandradarśanam occurs tomorrow, and followers of bōdhāyana/kātyāyana sūtras do not perform iṣṭiḥ on chandradarśanam day.

eacd5bbac4.b: Observed on Śukla-Prathamā tithi of Caitraḥ (lunar) month (Sūryōdayaḥ/puurvaviddha).
eacd5bbac4.s:
𑌶𑌰𑌤𑍍𑌕𑌾𑌲𑍇 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌪𑍂𑌜𑌾 𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌯𑌤𑍇 𑌯𑌾 𑌚 𑌵𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌷𑌿𑌕𑍀।  
𑌵𑌸𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌕𑌾𑌲𑍇 𑌸𑌾 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑍋𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌾 𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍈𑌃 𑌶𑍁𑌭𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌿𑌭𑌿𑌃॥  
---𑌮𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌕𑌣𑍍𑌡𑍇𑌯-𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑌮𑍍 (𑌸𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑌿𑌕𑍌𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁𑌭𑍇)

eada223706.b: Observed on Śukla-Trayōdaśī tithi of Jyaiṣṭhaḥ (lunar) month (Sūryōdayaḥ/puurvaviddha).
eada223706.s:
𑌜𑍍𑌯𑍇𑌷𑍍𑌠𑌶𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍋𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌦𑍌𑌰𑍍𑌭𑌾𑌗𑍍𑌯𑌶𑌮𑌨𑌂 𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌮𑍍॥௧௮॥  
𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌨𑌦𑍀𑌤𑍋𑌯𑍇 𑌪𑍂𑌜𑌯𑍇𑌚𑍍𑌛𑍁𑌚𑌿𑌦𑍇𑌶𑌜𑌮𑍍।  
𑌶𑍍𑌵𑍇𑌤𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌦𑌾𑌰𑌮𑌰𑍍𑌕𑌂 𑌵𑌾 𑌕𑌰𑌵𑍀𑌰𑌂 𑌚 𑌰𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌕𑌮𑍍॥௧௯॥  
𑌨𑌿𑌰𑍀𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌯 𑌗𑌗𑌨𑍇 𑌸𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌯𑍇𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌦𑌾।  
𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌦𑌾𑌰𑌕𑌰𑌵𑍀𑌰𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌕𑌾 𑌭𑌵𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍋 𑌭𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌕𑌰𑌾𑌂𑌶𑌜𑌾𑌃॥௨௦॥  
𑌪𑍂𑌜𑌿𑌤𑌾 𑌮𑌮 𑌦𑍌𑌰𑍍𑌭𑌾𑌗𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌨𑌾𑌶𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌨𑌮𑍋𑌽𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌵𑌃।  
𑌇𑌤𑍍𑌥𑌂 𑌯𑍋𑌽𑌰𑍍𑌚𑌯𑌤𑍇 𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌷𑍇 𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌷𑍇 𑌦𑍍𑌰𑍁𑌮𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑌮𑍍॥௨௧॥  
𑌨𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌤𑍇 𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌦𑍌𑌰𑍍𑌭𑌾𑌗𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌵𑌿𑌚𑌾𑌰𑌣𑌾॥   
---𑌨𑌾𑌰𑌦𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇 𑌬𑍃𑌹𑌨𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌰𑌦𑍀𑌯𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌭𑌾𑌗𑍇 𑌬𑍃𑌹𑌦𑍁𑌪𑌾𑌖𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌨𑍇 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑌶𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌸𑍍𑌥𑌿𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍋𑌦𑌶𑍀𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌕𑌥𑌨𑌂 𑌨𑌾𑌮 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌵𑌿𑌂𑌶𑌦𑌧𑌿𑌕𑌶𑌤𑌤𑌮𑍋𑌽𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌃

eb1f75edb5.b: Observed on Śukla-Aṣṭamī tithi of Vaiśākhaḥ (lunar) month (Aparāhṇaḥ/vyaapti). The event occurred in 3665 (Kali era).
eb1f75edb5.d: Śoṇagiri, son of Prabhākaraśarma, who lived on the banks of river Pinākinī, became Jagadguru Prajñāghana and attained blissful state on the night of the eighth day of the bright fortnight of the month of Vaiśāka in the year Subhānu/Svabhānu.
eb1f75edb5.s:
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌭𑌾𑌕𑌰𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌮𑌭𑌵𑌃 𑌪𑌿𑌨𑌾𑌕𑌿𑌨𑍀-  
𑌤𑌟𑍀𑌭𑌵𑌃 𑌶𑍋𑌣𑌗𑌿𑌰𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌜𑌗𑌦𑍍𑌗𑍁𑌰𑍁𑌃।  
𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌭𑌾𑌨𑍁𑌵𑍈𑌶𑌾𑌖𑌸𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌮𑍀𑌨𑌿𑌶𑌿  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌜𑍍𑌞𑌾𑌘𑌨𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌪 𑌪𑌰𑌂 𑌪𑌦𑌂 𑌮𑍁𑌦𑌾॥௫௫॥  
—𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌶𑍍𑌲𑍋𑌕𑌮𑌞𑍍𑌜𑌰𑍀

eb2b8af98f.d: Budhaḥ rises out of combustion (udayaH), heading prāk (east), on 2027-Jan-24 03:52. At this moment budhaḥ is at śraviṣṭhā-1 makaraḥ (latitude 1°30′36.32″ S, moving r̥ju (direct)), magnitude -1.01, elongation 14°18′44.27″ E of the Sun. Emergence from combustion restores a graha's full strength; this is generally considered an auspicious time to begin activities connected with budhaḥ's significations.

eb8d7f9289.b: Observed on Śukla-Caturthī tithi of Bhādrapadaḥ (lunar) month (Madhyāhnaḥ/puurvaviddha).
eb8d7f9289.s:
𑌸𑍁𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍁𑌵𑌾𑌚---  
𑌶𑌿𑌵𑌾 𑌶𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌾 𑌸𑍁𑌖𑌾 𑌰𑌾𑌜𑌂𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌥𑍀 𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌵𑌿𑌧𑌾 𑌸𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑌾।   
𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌿 𑌭𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌪𑌦𑍇 𑌶𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲𑌾 𑌶𑌿𑌵𑌾 𑌲𑍋𑌕𑍇𑌷𑍁 𑌪𑍂𑌜𑌿𑌤𑌾॥௧॥   
𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌦𑌾𑌨𑌮𑍁𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑍋 𑌜𑌪𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌥𑌾।   
𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌯𑌮𑌾𑌣𑌂 𑌶𑌤𑌗𑍁𑌣𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌸𑌾𑌦𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌦𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌨𑍋 𑌨𑍃𑌪॥௨॥   
𑌗𑍁𑌡𑌲𑌵𑌣𑌘𑍃𑌤𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌂 𑌤𑍁 𑌦𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌶𑍁𑌭𑌕𑌰𑌂 𑌸𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑌮𑍍।   
𑌗𑍁𑌡𑌾𑌪𑍂𑌪𑍈𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌵𑍀𑌰 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌣𑌭𑍋𑌜𑌨𑌮𑍍॥௩॥   
𑌯𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌨𑌰𑌶𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌦𑍂𑌲 𑌪𑍂𑌜𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌸𑌦𑌾 𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌯𑌃।   
𑌗𑍁𑌡𑌲𑌵𑌣𑌪𑍂𑌪𑍈𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍂𑌂 𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌶𑍁𑌰𑌮𑍇𑌵 𑌚॥௪॥   
𑌤𑌾𑌃 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌃 𑌸𑍁𑌭𑌗𑌾𑌃 𑌸𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍈 𑌵𑌿𑌘𑍍𑌨𑍇𑌶𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌨𑍁𑌮𑍋𑌦𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍍।   
𑌕𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌕𑌾 𑌤𑍁 𑌵𑌿𑌶𑍇𑌷𑍇𑌣 𑌵𑌿𑌧𑌿𑌨𑌾𑌽𑌨𑍇𑌨 𑌪𑍂𑌜𑌯𑍇𑌤𑍍॥௫॥   
---𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌭𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌯𑍇 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇 𑌶𑌤𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌧𑌸𑌾𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑌂𑌹𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌮𑍇 𑌪𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌣𑌿 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌥𑍀𑌕𑌲𑍍𑌪𑍇 𑌸𑍁𑌖𑌾𑌵𑌹𑌾𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌾𑌰𑌕𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌥𑍀𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌨𑌿𑌰𑍂𑌪𑌣𑌂 𑌨𑌾𑌮𑍈𑌕𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌂𑌶𑍋𑌽𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌤𑌃  
𑌅𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑍇𑌵 𑌚𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌦𑌰𑍍𑌶𑌨𑍇 𑌦𑍋𑌷𑌮𑌾𑌹 𑌪𑌰𑌾𑌶𑌰𑌃---   
𑌕𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌯𑍇 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌥𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌚 𑌶𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲𑍇 𑌚𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌦𑌰𑍍𑌶𑌨𑌮𑍍।   
𑌮𑌿𑌥𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌭𑌿𑌦𑍂𑌷𑌣𑌂 𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍 𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌪𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍇𑌨𑍍𑌨 𑌤𑌂 𑌸𑌦𑌾॥   
𑌤𑌦𑍍𑌦𑍋𑌷𑌶𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌯𑍇 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍋 𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇---   
𑌸𑌿𑌹𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌸𑍇𑌨𑌮𑌵𑌧𑍀𑌤𑍍 𑌸𑌿𑌂𑌹𑍋 𑌜𑌾𑌮𑍍𑌬𑌵𑌤𑌾 𑌹𑌤𑌃।   
𑌸𑍁𑌕𑍁𑌮𑌾𑌰𑌕 𑌮𑌾 𑌰𑍋𑌦𑍀𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌵 𑌹𑍍𑌯𑍇𑌷𑌃 𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌕𑌃॥

eba7d05614.b: Event occured on 1737-04-08 (gregorian). Julian date was converted to Gregorian in this reckoning.
eba7d05614.d:
One brother bAji rAv makes a dash to mogol Delhi, outmanoeuvring 2 armies; same day his younger bro chimAji appa readies to mount an attack on the Firangis.
The Badshah at Delhi slept secure in the thought that the large armies of Sadat, Bangash & Khan Dauran to his south would protect him. From Gwalior area, Bajirao rode 200 km in just 4 days avoiding all those armies & gatecrashed Delhi. Then, he defeated a well trained Mughal Army led by Amir Khan Bahadur.

ebf02ee287.d: Śukraḥ enters vArdhakya (old age) on 2027-Jun-25 22:05, 15 days before it sets into combustion (mAudhyam). At this moment śukraḥ is at mr̥gaśīrṣam-2 vr̥ṣabhaḥ (latitude 0°21′52.09″ S, moving r̥ju (direct)), magnitude -3.88, elongation 12°57′39.05″ W of the Sun. A graha in vArdhakya is considered weakened, giving reduced results, though less so than in outright mAudhya.

𑌵𑍈𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌵𑍈𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌚 𑌜𑌨𑌤𑌾𑌨𑌨𑍍𑌦𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌧𑌨𑌃॥  
𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌾𑌨𑌨𑍍𑌦𑌸𑌮𑍁𑌦𑍍𑌭𑍂𑌤𑌾 𑌦𑌿𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌦𑌮𑌨𑌮𑌞𑍍𑌜𑌰𑍀।

ec05155e57.b: Observed on Śukla-Daśamī tithi of Māghaḥ (lunar) month (Aparāhṇaḥ/vyaapti). The event occurred in 3273 (Kali era).
ec05155e57.d: The boy Īśvara, son of Ujjvala bhaṭṭa of Karnataka, known as Cidghana, who approached Sureśvara and acquired the knowledge of bhāṣyas etc., having got his (Sureśvara’s) responsibility and remaining in the Pīṭha there, this Cidghana spent forty-five years as if Śiva Himself had come there to grant liberation to those who seek liberation. Revered by the wise, Cidghana having placed Vātsyāyāna, the initiated who was hailed as Hari arrived from Milky Ocean, and imparting the precepts He had attained his form, the pure consciousness on the tenth day of the bright fortnight in the month of Māgha in the year Virodhikṛt of the Kali era.
ec05155e57.s:
𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌾𑌟𑍋𑌜𑍍𑌜𑍍𑌵𑌲𑌸𑍂𑌨𑍁𑌰𑍀𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌰𑌵𑌟𑍁𑌃 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌸𑍁𑌰𑍇𑌶𑌂 𑌚𑌿𑌰𑌾𑌤𑍍  
𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌭𑌾𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌪𑌲𑌭𑍍𑌯 𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌚 𑌧𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌯 𑌪𑍀𑌠𑍇 𑌵𑌸𑌨𑍍।  
𑌨𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌯𑍇 𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌶𑌿𑌵𑌾𑌃 (௪௫) 𑌸𑌮𑌾𑌃 𑌶𑌿𑌵 𑌇𑌵 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌯𑍋𑌽𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌿𑌨𑌾𑌂 𑌦𑍇𑌹𑌿𑌨𑌾𑌂  
𑌦𑌾𑌤𑍁𑌂 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌯 𑌉𑌪𑌾𑌗𑌤𑍋𑌽𑌯𑌮𑌿𑌵 𑌯𑌃 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌚𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌘𑌨𑌾𑌖𑍍𑌯𑍋 𑌬𑌭𑍌॥௨௧॥  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌂 𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍀𑌰𑌸𑌰𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌟𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌰𑌿𑌰𑌿𑌤𑌿 𑌖𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌤𑌂 𑌚 𑌵𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌨𑌂  
𑌪𑍀𑌠𑍇 𑌸𑍍𑌵𑍇 𑌵𑌿𑌨𑌿𑌵𑍇𑌶𑍍𑌯 𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌨𑌿𑌯𑌮𑌂 𑌸𑌞𑍍𑌚𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌯 𑌚 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌯𑌾𑌮𑍍।  
𑌕𑌲𑍍𑌯𑌬𑍍𑌦𑍇 𑌚 𑌵𑌿𑌰𑍋𑌧𑌿𑌕𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌨𑍁𑌤𑌪𑌃 𑌶𑍁𑌦𑍍𑌧𑍇 𑌦𑌶𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑌗𑌾𑌤𑍍  
𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌂 𑌰𑍂𑌪𑌂 𑌪𑌰𑌮𑌂 𑌸𑍁𑌧𑍀𑌶𑌤𑌨𑍁𑌤𑌃 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌚𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌘𑌨𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌘𑌨𑌮𑍍॥௨௨॥  
—𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌶𑍍𑌲𑍋𑌕𑌮𑌞𑍍𑌜𑌰𑍀

ec09b0bb94.d: Budhaḥ sets into combustion (astamayaH), heading prāk (east), on 2025-May-13 04:31. At this moment budhaḥ is at aśvinī-4 mēṣaḥ (latitude 2°09′27.23″ S, moving r̥ju (direct)), magnitude -0.55, elongation 18°21′42.68″ W of the Sun. Combustion (mAudhyam) is generally considered to weaken a graha's ability to give full results in its significations; undertakings connected with budhaḥ are traditionally best avoided until it re-emerges.

𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌣𑌾𑌯 𑌦𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌤𑌿 𑌬𑍋𑌧𑌾𑌯𑌨𑌃।

𑌦𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑍍 𑌵𑌿𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌯 𑌰𑌾𑌜𑍇𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌪𑌤𑍍𑌸𑌮𑍃𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌯𑍇॥

ec70bd8cca.b: Observed on Mūlā nakshatra of Siṁhaḥ (sidereal solar) month (Prātaḥ/paraviddha).
ec70bd8cca.d:
Between the 6th and 9th centuries, in South India, there existed 63 ardent devotees of Bhagavan Shiva, collectively known as the Nayanmars. These devout individuals, hailing from various walks of life including potters, fishermen, farmers, merchants, priests, hunters, and washermen, created devotional songs still sung by followers around the globe. Among these Nayanmars, Appar, Sambandar, and Sundarar, known for their Thevaram hymns, along with Manikkavasagar, are distinguished as the Samayacharyas or the ‘The Four’ (nālvar) revered teachers of the faith. They were instrumental in promoting the Shaiva Siddhanta philosophy and culture, effectively challenging the spread of Jainism and Buddhism. Their teachings centered around the concept that Shiva embodies love, and that embracing love for all beings and existence is essential in connecting with Shiva, the Supreme Being.

Kungiliya Kalaya Nayanmar, a Brahmana from Tirukadavur in the Chola kingdom, was renowned for his devotion to Bhagavan Shiva, symbolised by his constant burning of incense before the deity. The temple in Tirukadavur housed the Amrita Lingam, which originated from a pot of nectar transformed into a Lingam. The temple's deity, Amrita Ghateshwarar, was worshipped by Markandeya, leading to his immortality. The Devi of the temple, Abhirami Amman, was venerated by Abhirami Bhattar, whose devotion led to a miraculous transformation of the moon's phase.

Despite experiencing sudden poverty, Nayanmar continued his devotion, even selling his property to maintain his ritual of burning incense. One day, his wife, willing to support his devotion, offered her sacred Mangalyam to sell for food. However, when Nayanmar went to sell it, he was so captivated by the offer of high-quality incense from a hawker (Bhagavan Shiva in disguise) that he exchanged the Mangalyam for it, forgetting his family's hunger.

Bhagavan Shiva, impressed with the couple's devotion, blessed them with wealth. Nayanmar's wife prepared a meal and awaited his return. When Nayanmar went to the temple with the incense, Bhagavan Shiva appeared to him, acknowledging his devotion and instructing him to return home. Astonished, Nayanmar found his house transformed into a place of prosperity and shared his newfound wealth with other Shiva Bhaktas.

Nayanmar's devotion was further exemplified in Tiruppanandal (https://maps.app.goo.gl/Du84NWnVhaTQWMYE8), where he straightened the leaning Lingam of Arunasatesar, which had tilted to accept a garland from a devotee. Using a rope of divine love, Nayanmar miraculously righted the Lingam, a feat that astonished and earned him further reverence.

After spending more time serving Bhagavan Shiva and His devotees, Nayanmar eventually attained the divine abode, leaving a legacy of unwavering devotion and service to Bhagavan.
ec70bd8cca.r: - 63 Nayanmar Saints by Swami Sivananda, published by The Divine Life Society

ecb57c7a24.d:
On this day, in the first battle on the neDuMkoTa coast-to-mountain fortification, Tipu Sultan and troops were routed. Tipu was wounded (physically and mentally), and lost 1k troops. padmanAbhapura lost 300. Several of Tipu's officers (including Europeans) were captured.

Two horses were shot from under Tipu, and he even got an arrow in the back. During the hasty retreat, Tipu fell back into the ditch twice before being helped out and the occasional lameness which he suffered until his death was reputedly the consequence. Tipu's sword, the palanquin, the dagger, the ring and many other personal effects fell into the ditch, and then into the hands of the minister keshava-dAsa.


Aftermath
Humiliated Tipu vowed to take down "the contemptible wall". The fine wall held up till 15th April. Then he managed a 1km wide breach after 1 month of sustained artillery fire and poured in - only to be foiled again at Alwaye river bank. He retreated by 24 May 1790 to defend his kingdom from British threat.

Context
The Dutch captive-turned general of padmanAbhapura's mArtANDa varma, De Lannoy, had built an excellent fortification from coast to mountain - neDuMkoTa. It had a 16 feet wide and 20 deep ditch. dharmarAja rAma varma had tried to get British help when Tipu's attack was imminent, but only got words. The Dutch, who'd sold forts to rAma varma helped a bit - by sending an engineer von Krause, who was dispatched to the wall. He wrote an account of the battle.

When Tipu attacked, he tried filling a small portion of the ditch with cotton sacks and moving in a small column via a narrow passage. At first the Mysoreans overpowered three batteries of the Lines but subsequently their flanks were subjected to fire from the woods. They were so surprised by the first round of fire that they fell into disorder. Then the well drilled nair army advanced and the confusion increased. Those Mysoreans who had not yet been trampled down by their horses while retreating found that the sacks with cotton, used for filling up the ditch when they set out, as well as some powder-barrels, had caught fire. This forced them to jump from the ramparts.

ecfe187da6.d:
On this day, vAnchinathan Iyer, inspired by  Subramaniam Aiyar and armed by Va Ve Su Iyer accomplice of nIlakaNTha brahmachAri of bhAratamAta-sangha with a gun sent by sAvarkar's accompalice Madam Cama of Paris Indian Society, shot dead a mlecCha collector Robert Ashe (who had successfully harrassed VO Chidambaram Pillai's Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company) before killing himself (after pushing away his peon Khadar bAdshAh). His letter:

- I dedicate my life as a small contribution to my motherland. I am alone responsible for this.
- The mlechas of England having captured our country, tread over the sanathana dharma of the Hindus and destroy them. Every Indian is trying to drive out the English and get swarajyam and restore sanathana dharma. Our Raman, Sivaji, Krishnan, Guru Govindan, Arjuna ruled our land protecting all dharmas, but in this land, they are making arrangements to crown George V, a mlecha, and one who eats the flesh of cows.
- Three thousand Madrasees have taken a vow to kill George V as soon as he lands in our country. In order to make others know our intention, I who am the least in the company, have done this deed this day. This is what everyone in Hindustan should consider it as his duty.
- I will kill Ashe, whose arrival here is to celebrate the crowning of cow-eater King George V in this glorious land which was once ruled by great samrats. This I do to make them understand the fate of those who cherish the thought of enslaving this sacred land.
- I, as the least of them, wish to warn George by killing Ashe. 
- Vande Mataram. Vande Mataram. Vande Mataram
- sd/-, R. Vanchi Aiyar, Shencottah

eeae687033.d:
Between the 6th and 9th centuries, in South India, there existed 63 ardent devotees of Bhagavan Shiva, collectively known as the Nayanmars. These devout individuals, hailing from various walks of life including potters, fishermen, farmers, merchants, priests, hunters, and washermen, created devotional songs still sung by followers around the globe. Among these Nayanmars, Appar, Sambandar, and Sundarar, known for their Thevaram hymns, along with Manikkavasagar, are distinguished as the Samayacharyas or the ‘The Four’ (nālvar) revered teachers of the faith. They were instrumental in promoting the Shaiva Siddhanta philosophy and culture, effectively challenging the spread of Jainism and Buddhism. Their teachings centered around the concept that Shiva embodies love, and that embracing love for all beings and existence is essential in connecting with Shiva, the Supreme Being.

Tirumula Nayanmar, a revered Shaiva Siddha and one of the eight disciples of Tirunandi Devar, embarked on a journey to meet Agastya Rishi in the Pothia hills. Departing from Kailasa, he visited numerous Shaivite shrines and, upon reaching Tiruvavaduthurai, witnessed a herd of mourning cows beside their deceased herder, Mulan. To comfort the cows, Tirumula Nayanmar transferred his consciousness into Mulan's body, leaving his own physical form in a tree trunk.

Assuming Mulan's role, he herded the cows back to the village, where Mulan's wife, expecting her husband, was surprised by his changed demeanor. Declaring himself a changed person and advising her to seek spiritual liberation, Tirumula Nayanmar distanced himself from her, arousing the village's curiosity. Upon investigation, the villagers acknowledged his spiritual transformation and advised the wife to respect his new path.

Unable to retrieve his original body owing to Bhagavan Shiva's Lila, Tirumula Nayanmar, still in Mulan's form, dedicated himself to composing a seminal work on Shaiva Philosophy at Tiruvavaduthurai. He devoted himself to worshiping Bhagavan and settled beneath a nearby peepal tree, entering a state of deep meditation. He remained in this state of Samadhi for three millennia. However, each year, he momentarily emerged from this deep meditative state to compose a single verse. Over the span of three thousand years, this process led to the creation of three thousand verses, collectively forming the sacred text known as the Tirumandiram. Having accomplished his divine mission, Tirumula Nayanmar returned to Kailasa.

𑌸 𑌕𑌾𑌲𑍋 𑌵𑌿𑌜𑌯𑍋 𑌜𑍍𑌞𑍇𑌯𑌃 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌸𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌯𑍇॥ (𑌜𑍍𑌯𑍋𑌤𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌨𑌿𑌬𑌨𑍍𑌧𑌃)  
𑌸𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑌿-𑌕𑍌𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁𑌭𑍇---  
𑌅𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑍇𑌵 𑌦𑌶𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌵𑌿𑌜𑌯𑌮𑍁𑌹𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌪𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌦𑍇𑌶𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌰𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌿𑌭𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾 𑌵𑌿𑌧𑍇𑌯𑌾---  
𑌆𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌨𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌸𑌿𑌤𑍇 𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇 𑌦𑌶𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌰𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌷𑍁।  
𑌸𑌾𑌯𑌙𑍍𑌕𑌾𑌲𑍇 𑌶𑍁𑌭𑌾 𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾 𑌦𑌿𑌵𑌾 𑌵𑌾 𑌵𑌿𑌜𑌯𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌣𑍇॥  
𑌇𑌤𑌿 𑌭𑍃𑌗𑍁𑌵𑌚𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍍।  
𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍇𑌤𑌿 𑌚𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌨𑍁𑌕𑍂𑌲𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌨𑌾𑌪𑍇𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌮𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌶𑌯𑌃।  
𑌈𑌷𑌤𑍍 𑌸𑌨𑍍𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑌤𑌿𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌃 𑌕𑌿𑌞𑍍𑌚𑌿𑌦𑍁𑌦𑍍𑌭𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌨𑌤𑌾𑌰𑌕𑌃।  
𑌵𑌿𑌜𑌯𑍋 𑌨𑌾𑌮 𑌕𑌾𑌲𑍋𑌽𑌯𑌂 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌸𑌾𑌧𑌕𑌃॥  
𑌇𑌤𑌿 𑌜𑍍𑌯𑍋𑌤𑌿 𑌶𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍋𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌵𑌿𑌜𑌯𑌮𑍁𑌹𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌭𑌿𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌯𑌂 𑌸𑌾𑌯𑌮𑌿𑌤𑌿।  
𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍋 𑌮𑍁𑌹𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌤𑍋𑌽𑌪𑌿 𑌵𑌿𑌜𑌯𑌃 𑌪𑌰𑌿𑌕𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌤𑌃।  
𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍈𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌧𑌾𑌤𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾 𑌵𑌿𑌜𑌯𑌕𑌾𑌙𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌿𑌭𑌿𑌃॥  
𑌇𑌤𑌿 𑌭𑍃𑌗𑍂𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌵𑌿𑌜𑌯𑌮𑍁𑌹𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌨𑍁𑌕𑍂𑌲𑍍𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌶𑌯𑌂 𑌦𑌿𑌵𑌾 𑌵𑍇𑌤𑌿।  
𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍀𑌯𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌉𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌮𑍁𑌹𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌤𑍇𑌽𑌪𑌿 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌸𑍍𑌥𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌨 𑌵𑌿𑌧𑍇𑌯𑌮𑍍।  
𑌦𑌶𑌮𑍀 𑌯𑌃 𑌸𑌮𑍁𑌲𑍍𑌲𑌙𑍍𑌘𑍍𑌯 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌸𑍍𑌥𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍁𑌤𑍇 𑌨𑌰𑌃।  
𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌸𑌂𑌵𑌤𑍍𑌸𑌰𑌂 𑌰𑌾𑌜𑍍𑌯𑍇 𑌨 𑌕𑍋𑌽𑌪𑌿 𑌵𑌿𑌜𑌯𑍋 𑌭𑌵𑍇𑌤𑍍॥  
𑌇𑌤𑌿 𑌸𑍍𑌕𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌦𑌨𑌿𑌷𑍇𑌧𑌾𑌤𑍍।

𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌪𑍂𑌜𑌯𑍇𑌦𑍍𑌦𑍇𑌵𑍀𑌂 𑌶𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌮𑍍॥  
𑌵𑍇𑌦𑍇𑌷𑍁 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌶𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌷𑍁 𑌦𑌿𑌵𑌿 𑌭𑍂𑌮𑍌 𑌰𑌸𑌾𑌤𑌲𑍇।  
𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍁𑌤𑍋 𑌦𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌬𑌹𑍁𑌶𑍋 𑌨 𑌶𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌰𑌹𑌿𑌤𑌃 𑌶𑌿𑌵𑌃।  
𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌂 𑌶𑌕𑍍𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌂 𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌧𑌾 𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌹𑌾 𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌂 𑌸𑌾𑌵𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍀 𑌸𑌰𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌤𑍀।  
𑌪𑌤𑌿𑌂 𑌦𑍇𑌹𑌿 𑌸𑍁𑌤𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍇𑌹𑌿 𑌗𑍃𑌹𑌂 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌿 𑌨𑌮𑍋𑌽𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌤𑍇॥  
𑌯𑍋𑌷𑌿𑌤𑌃 𑌪𑍁𑌰𑍁𑌷𑍋 𑌵𑌾𑌽𑌪𑌿 𑌖𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌤𑌂 𑌰𑌮𑍍𑌭𑌾𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌂 𑌭𑍁𑌵𑌿।  
𑌭𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌪𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌂 𑌗𑍃𑌹𑌂 𑌭𑍋𑌗𑌾𑌨𑍍 𑌕𑍁𑌲𑌵𑍃𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌿𑌮𑌵𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌨𑍁𑌯𑍁𑌃॥  
-𑌸𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑌿-𑌕𑍌𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁𑌭𑌃  
𑌸𑌾 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌵𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌾 𑌗𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌯𑌾।

ef5a78b4ef.b: Partial lunar eclipse (parimāṇa ≈4.1 of 12 aṅgulas), Moon at the Rahu node (puccha/descending).
ef5a78b4ef.d: The eclipse is already in progress at moonrise (grastodaya). Umbral magnitude: 0.34 (parimāṇa ≈4.1 of the traditional 12 aṅgulas). Avoid food: 09:32►19:53 (from 3 yaamas before the yaama of first contact, until the eclipse's end). Those with janma nakshatra maghā/pūrvaphalgunī/uttaraphalgunī (preceding/grahaNa/succeeding), or pūrvāṣāḍhā (anujanma) or apabharaṇī (trijanma) get ashubha phala and should consider graha-shanti next day. By rashi: siṁhaḥ, kanyā, makaraḥ, vr̥ṣabhaḥ get more ashubha phala, dhanuḥ, kumbhaḥ, mēṣaḥ, karkaṭaḥ somewhat ashubha, tulā, vr̥śchikaḥ, mīnaḥ, mithunam shubha phala. General notes: Avoid touching anything other than what's needed for the anushthana (especially bed/mat/cloth) until the mokSha snAna after the eclipse ends -- this is grahaNa Ashaucham. Do not sleep or attend to natural impulses during the eclipse. Mantra japa and dAna during the puNya kAla are of immense benefit. Do not view the eclipse with naked eyes. Pregnant women should avoid exposure to the sun/moon's light during the respective eclipse.
ef5a78b4ef.r: - Food-restriction timing and graha-shanti nakshatra/rashi lists follow this pancAnga's "General notes for all grahanas" instructions.

ef6bb94e1d.d: Śukraḥ rises out of combustion (udayaH), heading prāk (east), on 2026-Feb-20 13:13. At this moment śukraḥ is at śatabhiṣak-4 kumbhaḥ (latitude 1°27′02.75″ S, moving r̥ju (direct)), magnitude -3.90, elongation 10°48′09.26″ E of the Sun. Emergence from combustion restores a graha's full strength; this is generally considered an auspicious time to begin activities connected with śukraḥ's significations.

ef95e73f1e.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between aṅgārakaḥ and budhaḥ in uttarāṣāḍhā makaraḥ, center-to-center separation 0°57′45.22″.
ef95e73f1e.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°57′45.22″, 0°57′40.91″ apart, disc-to-disc. aṅgārakaḥ at uttarāṣāḍhā-2 makaraḥ (latitude 0°59′15.10″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude +1.08, elongation 2°22′18.86″ W). budhaḥ at uttarāṣāḍhā-2 makaraḥ (latitude 1°57′00.32″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -1.24, elongation 2°54′24.13″ W). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here budhaḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) budhaḥ is taken as jayI over aṅgārakaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

efcbfa9a21.d: Special vrata day for Ganesha. In this month, Ganesha is worshipped as kr̥ṣṇapiṅgala-mahāgaṇapatiḥ. Fast during the day and pray to Ganesha after moonrise, chanting the shloka mentioned.
efcbfa9a21.s:
𑌗𑌣𑌾𑌧𑌿𑌪𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌂 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑍇𑌶 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌥𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌪𑍂𑌜𑌿𑌤𑍋 𑌮𑌯𑌾।  
𑌕𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌂 𑌮𑍋𑌚𑌯𑍇𑌶𑌾𑌨 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌮𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌂 𑌚 𑌦𑍇𑌹𑌿 𑌮𑍇॥  
  
𑌯𑌦𑌾 𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌲𑍇𑌶𑌿𑌤𑍋 𑌮𑌰𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑍋 𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌦𑍁𑌃𑌖𑍈𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌦𑌾𑌰𑍁𑌣𑍈𑌃।

effed99ff4.b: Observed on Śukla-Aṣṭamī tithi of Caitraḥ (lunar) month (Sūryōdayaḥ/puurvaviddha).
effed99ff4.s:
𑌸𑍍𑌕𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍇---  
𑌚𑍈𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍇 𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌿 𑌸𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌯𑍋 𑌨𑌰𑍋 𑌨𑌿𑌯𑌤𑍇𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌯𑌃।  
𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌲𑍍𑌲𑍌𑌹𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌤𑍋𑌯𑍇𑌷𑍁 𑌸 𑌯𑌾𑌤𑌿 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌣𑌃 𑌪𑌦𑌮𑍍॥  
𑌲𑍌𑌹𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌯𑍋 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌪𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌃। 𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌕𑌲𑍍𑌪𑌃---  
𑌓𑌮𑌦𑍍𑌯𑍇𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑌿 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌪𑌾𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌯𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌕𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌪𑌦𑌗𑌮𑌨𑌕𑌾𑌮𑍋 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌪𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌮𑌹𑌂 𑌕𑌰𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌯𑍇 𑌇𑌤𑌿।  
𑍐 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌪𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌭𑌾𑌗 𑌶𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌨𑍋𑌃 𑌕𑍁𑌲𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌭𑌵।  
𑌅𑌮𑍋𑌘𑌾𑌗𑌰𑍍𑌭𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌭𑌤 𑌪𑌾𑌪𑌂 𑌲𑍌𑌹𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌯 𑌮𑍇 𑌹𑌰॥  
𑌇𑌤𑌿 𑌪𑌠𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍।
